Fortunately I have arranged a much better internet connection (it's still a bit slow though), but most of my college friends still suffer.

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-08-01 18:51 UTC

## extreme manual install

*2016-08-01 to 2016-08-01 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/extreme.20manual.20install/with/10339)*

**Eklavya Sharma** · 2016-08-01 18:51 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-08-01 18:51 UTC

interesting -- is there a `wget` alternative we could be using?

**Eklavya Sharma** · 2016-08-01 18:54 UTC

**Christie Koehler** · 2016-08-01 18:56 UTC

Was it not reliable because it had no way to resume interrupted downloads?

**Eklavya Sharma** · 2016-08-01 18:57 UTC

I don't remember.

**GervaisdeM** · 2016-08-01 22:52 UTC

I've never had issues with wget, but curl could be an alternative. It can also resume downloads if they fail.

Are you familiar with sha digests?  I didn't write this code, so I'm not 100% sure of the intent, but my reading of the code is that we are caching venvs for particular instances of the requirements files, and we use the sha digest to name the directory.

**Steve Howell** · 2016-09-28 03:28 UTC

a sha is sort of conceptually similar to a guid, if you happen to know what a guid is

**Steve Howell** · 2016-09-28 03:30 UTC

That analogy may be more confusing than helpful.  Basically, a sha digest maps some unique set of data to a simpler number that can be used like an id.

**Steve Howell** · 2016-09-28 03:31 UTC

For example, d975c41c948e2f511fb1e9d50e4fec77094ba8c4 refers to basically one string of git commits in the universe, unless there's some incredibly remarkable coincidence.

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-10-11 06:45 UTC

OK, here's I think what's going on:
* `pip` has a bug where anything installed after talon gets the `--no-ml` option passed to it incorrectly
* before, talon happened to always be last because it is the alphabetically latest of the dependencies installed from git (or maybe something about the topology combined with that)
* The change to install the Zulip API bindings by default, de5b6d9e37831e4afd4b1fb87a55a1e6e55cc589, added a new thing that was installed after talon, since things installed with `-e` are apparently processed last
* I was confused about the cause because earlier in my branch, I had tried switching talon to install from pypi, which made the problem worse by causing other things to be installed after talon (and in particular made reverting de5b6d9e37831e4afd4b1fb87a55a1e6e55cc589 not fix the problem).

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-10-11 06:45 UTC

So, yeah, Umair, your proposal should solve the problem for us by making us not need that option.

## Recent upgrades

*2016-10-16 to 2016-11-01 · 22 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Recent.20upgrades/with/39119)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-10-16 08:31 UTC

I've gotten a few recent reports that provisioning is still often really slow when one upgrades across a week of Zulip development.  Having investigated the code in some detail, I've determined that there was a bug in our logic in scripts/lib/setup_venv.py for determining whether we can reuse packages from an existing virtualenv when we update our dependencies: `get_package_names` doesn't correctly handle our dependencies that are pinned to git versions (basically it ends up comparing the git commit IDs, in addition to the package names).  This means whenever we update the version of one of those, we can't use the virtualenv copying logic and thus end up reinstalling all the dependencies.  

I believe I've fixed that via https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/fcde846b5864e34ac49b5ad8c398c493c9ce93a0, so hopefully starting on your second provision from now after you rebase onto master this will be a lot better (because of the nature of the bug, it won't help until the second provision).

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-10-16 08:32 UTC

@Steve Howell FYI

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-10-16 08:34 UTC

Also FYI, I merged a big upgrade to our markdown processor which will mean that you need to provision in order for the tests to pass the next time you rebase onto master.

## api/zulip/ installation issues

*2016-12-13 to 2017-01-07 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/api.2Fzulip.2F.20installation.20issues/with/92011)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-12-13 19:13 UTC

Hey folks, so I wanted to talk about how we should install the Zulip API bindings in the Zulip development environment

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-12-13 19:13 UTC

Currently, we are using the `-e api/` feature of the `requirements.txt` files (really, feature of `pip`) in `requirements/dev.txt` to install this

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-12-13 19:15 UTC

This feature is intended to make it super nice when you're developing a module because it'll use the copy in your source tree

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-12-13 19:16 UTC

However, this causes 2 problems:
* For some reason, putting the `.egg-info` files created into .gitignore causes Travis CI to fail
* In Travis CI and in development environments, we sometimes get provisioning failures related to those `.egg-info` files being there

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-12-13 19:23 UTC

One potential solution is to change the `requirements.txt` entry to just be `api/`, which would install it without live-updating

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-12-13 19:28 UTC

I'm going to test that out, I guess; we don't change the API bindings often, and I guess in theory we can resolve this by including the hashes of `api/` in what is used to determine whether we need to make a new virtualenv

**Tim Abbott** · 2016-12-13 19:55 UTC

OK I merged c77b1b2ac045a07521ab8b98a86c68a3359e28bf, which should help with this significantly

@Tim Abbott 
You were right that we misdiagnosed the root cause. The statement i suggested to add would have been worthless. 
Now then when i gave a thought that how the problem could have crept in, i figured out the 
the `.pgpass` file must have acquired its `sudo` ownership in container when i ran the provision from inside container using `sudo` initially when there was a error for some write permissions.Then you suggested that its is not to be run using `sudo` and must be some permission issue in container host.

## symlinks error

*2017-01-29 to 2017-09-12 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/symlinks.20error/with/140408)*

**Maydha K** · 2017-01-29 04:45 UTC

Hi, I'm trying to setup my dev environment (on Windows using Git Bash) and the provision step is erroring out early for me, complaining so:
   "Error: Unable to create symlinks. Make sure you have permission to create symbolic links."
I have already done everything in https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dev-env-first-time-contributors.html#os-symlink-error
If I do 'vagrant ssh' I can successfully create symbolic links (in the guest VM) in general using "ln -s" so I'm not sure what is wrong.  Any help will be appreciated.

**Akash Kothawale** · 2017-01-29 05:17 UTC

Have you enabled Windows symlinks in your Git BASH?
If `git config core.symlinks` returns `false` run `git config --global core.symlinks true` to set it.

Ideally this should be done before you clone zulip

**Maydha K** · 2017-01-29 05:25 UTC

Thanks for your response. Yes, already did that before cloning (it returned true)

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-01-29 05:28 UTC

Are you running as an administrator user?

**Maydha K** · 2017-01-29 05:35 UTC

Yes, I'm running as Administrator. One thing I see strangely is that if I do 'git config core.symlinks' it returns true in every directory but returns false if I invoke it in the zulip directory (the one I cloned into).  If I cd into the zulip  dir, then I cannot seem to set the core.symlinks flag to true at all even by doing 'git config --global core.symlinks true'

**Maydha K** · 2017-01-29 06:11 UTC

I think Windows was the culprit... I did not have privilege to create symlinks everywhere by default and git clone seemed to be picking up on it(?) Weirdly though I could create them in my home dir in the guest VM!  I have Windows 10 home edition so getting myself the create-symlinks priv was even more complicated. I had to use a third-party program called polsedit.  Now my provision succeeded. Hope this helps someone else.  :-)

I ran symlinks commands on git bash and others on windows cmd. Is the error raised because of this.

@MRIDU BHATNAGAR can you explain the problem in more detail?  I don't understand.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-12 11:18 UTC

In theory, those repositories should have been added automatically by `scripts/lib/setup-apt-repo`.  You can try doing `vagrant ssh` and then running `scripts/lib/setup-apt-repo` to debug.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-12 11:18 UTC

@CHOCOS to make sure you see this.

**Vishnu KS** · 2017-09-12 13:50 UTC

While I was in college yesterday a junior of mine encountered a similar error I think. He got it fixed by running `sudo apt-get update`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-12 13:51 UTC

Interesting.  We run that as part of `setup-apt-repo`, but maybe there's a bug where if `apt-get update` fails (due to network proxy issues or whatever), we won't rerun it properly the next time you try to provision.  I'll read the code a bit.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-12 13:52 UTC

Yeah, that's the bug.  `setup-apt-repo` doesn't rerun the setup stuff next time if `apt-get update` fails.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-12 14:09 UTC

Fixed in 600b164130f912d7a3f94111d55b6e80c6651a21

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-12 14:10 UTC

@CHOCOS you'll need to rebase, `sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/zulip.list`, and then re-provision to fix this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-12 14:10 UTC

Sorry for the  trouble, and thanks for posting those logs!  This was a subtle provisioning issue introduced by some caching work we did a few months ago, and I'm glad to have it resolved.

**Paul Weaver** · 2017-05-23 14:59 UTC

Couple of things I am concerned about:
1) That downloaded scripts installs yarn to a user's home directory. By linking it to /url/local/bin that could have weird consequences to other users in a muli-user system.
2) We want to ensure that the same version on yarn is installed so the script should be run every time (The downloaded script does a version check and terminates if the correct version is installed. -- If we want to avoid a network roundtrip to fetch the bash script we could check it in to the zulip repository.

**Paul Weaver** · 2017-05-23 17:04 UTC

I stuffed a copy of the install script in the repo so it should be idempotent and not require network if yarn is installed correctly.

## avoid --force while rebasing

*2017-06-05 to 2017-06-07 · 33 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/avoid.20--force.20while.20rebasing/with/219265)*

**Maxim Averin** · 2017-06-05 13:34 UTC

At Zulip we all use rebase-philosophy. But I have one problem. When you develop at your feature branch, make commits but when you want `git push origin feature`. Git rejects as someone add new commits. You can do `push` with `--force`,  but  it rewrites whole hoitory and can be harmful for other developers has this branch. **Question:** How to avoid this?
Internet and stackoverflow gives some bad solutions as deleting branch and create new with rebased code.

**Aditya Bansal** · 2017-06-05 14:08 UTC

I guess I do not follow you correctly. Why would other developers have your feature branch? I guess the workflow is something like this:
* Create a branch to work upon off master. (I guess this is what you mean by feature branch)
* Add new commits to it.
* Try `git pull --rebase upstream master` to check out if some new commits were merged to master.
* Push changes to your fork of repo on github using `git push origin branch-name`.

Now it sometimes might happen that we edited out commits or edited our last commit. When now we push to it will reject the commits. Here we use `--force`option to push the commits. But I guess since this is your own branch with commits made by you and other developers won't be having it.

**Maxim Averin** · 2017-06-05 14:43 UTC

Yeah, I agree with you. Situation when your branch is using by others developers is rare and only happens when you are totally stuck.

**Tommy Ip** · 2017-06-05 14:43 UTC

In addition, force push doesn't rewrite the **whole** history, only the commits that you are rebasing.

**Tommy Ip** · 2017-06-05 14:44 UTC

For public branches we should only do revert commits

**Maxim Averin** · 2017-06-05 14:44 UTC

yes, sure.

**Maxim Averin** · 2017-06-05 14:47 UTC

if we are talking not about Zulip, what do you think about this: use rebase if you do things locally, if it goes public you can use `merge` in some rare situation or  only `revert`? And what do you mean by revert? revert to which commit?

**Tommy Ip** · 2017-06-05 14:48 UTC

**Rein Zustand** · 2017-06-05 14:55 UTC

There is a caveat in git where someone who breaks into a repo to obtain a commit access to a canonical branch could rewrite the history instead of revert a change  immutably. It is a lot harder to do `--force` in Darcs by design, but still doable. There still needs to be a kind of incentive mechanism to maintain the canonical branch as a public log that is not specified in any vcs.

**Alex Dehnert** · 2017-06-05 22:58 UTC

> yeah i meant like in general why would someone who has grabbed enough experience to be a committer in public project even do it.

For compliance reasons (SOX, PCI, something) my company requires code review before merging code. One way to make that easy to check is to use an option like "only allow pushing to a branch by merging PRs". You can leave only a handful of people with admin permissions to change that setting, and all the devs will need to go through the PR workflow. (This is basically the model we're planning on, though we're not using Github for it.)

I mean, also, settings like this are useful for protecting against mistakes -- it's easy to, say, accidentally type / fetch from history `git push dehnert +foo` instead of `git push origin +foo`.

    for sha1sum in os.listdir(VENV_CACHE_PATH):

        # We only consider using using old virtualenvs that only

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-01-22 02:29 UTC

So, in line 474 of the settings.py file, changing, 

("SECRET_KEY", "") to ("SECRET_KEY", "1")

solved the failed provision.

```
  default: + scripts/lib/clean-unused-caches
    default: Cleaning unused venv caches...
    default: Cleaning unused node modules caches...
    default: Cleaning unused emoji caches...
    default: writing to /srv/zulip/var/36276b3f-04a2-4d3e-b7e0-1758b9ded62e/provision_version
    default: 
    default: Zulip development environment setup succeeded!
```

I am wondering why I would get an error with an empty string as the parameter? Thank you.

**Puneeth Chaganti** · 2019-01-22 04:17 UTC

Django doesn't like the `SECRET_KEY` being empty for security reasons. 

Ideally, you shouldn't have to make any changes, and provisioning should work without any changes needed on your end. The secrets file is generated during provisioning, and may be something went wrong while creating it.  If you have the logs of the provisioning, may be you can look through them to see if something went wrong. It may also be worth running provisioning again.

**Josh Klar** · 2022-12-30 03:20 UTC

As long as the docker daemon is running, that should be sufficient (and the errors are coming from the Docker stages, so we're good in that regard)

Bandwidth is one factor of the equation, but another factor is general robustness and reliability. ssl3 failing to read bytes often means the link between you and the server on the other end got interrupted somehow, or is perhaps entirely unreachable via one's ISP. **Rhea Parekh** · 2017-09-27 19:17 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-27 20:01 UTC

@Rhea just run `rm -f var/apt_dependencies_hash` and try provisioning again; I think that will fix it.

**Rhea Parekh** · 2017-09-27 20:10 UTC

@Tim Abbott It is still failing. I am getting the same error.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-27 22:44 UTC

@Rhea what happens if you run `apt-get update` inside the VM?  The actual problem here is that your system has a broken apt cache, and `apt-get update` needs to be run.

**Rhea Parekh** · 2017-09-27 23:29 UTC

@Tim Abbott That worked. Thank you so much!

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-27 23:55 UTC

On the broader issue of making this Just Work for folks, I feel like we should have a better system for handling that sort of situation in `provision`.  Possibly `provision --force` should do that unconditionally and be earlier in our list of things for people to try.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-27 23:55 UTC

Or maybe we should catch an error in that line and auto-recover with `apt-get update`?  Might be a better idea.

**Sean Miller** · 2017-09-28 00:59 UTC

Catching the error and rerunning apt-get update would have fixed at least one of my issues when provisioning yep.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-28 01:04 UTC

OK, cool, that seems like the right plan, then.  Are either of you interested in working on it @Rhea @Sean Miller?  I don't have time right now to investigate but I think it should be doable following the existing patterns in `tools/lib/provision.py`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-28 01:04 UTC

If not we should open an issue so this idea doesn't get lost.

**Rhea Parekh** · 2017-09-28 15:41 UTC

@Tim Abbott I would like to work on this. I'll start going through tools/lib/provision.py and try to backtrace the problem.

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-28 16:32 UTC

Sounds good :)

**Rhea Parekh** · 2017-09-29 05:08 UTC

@Tim Abbott  I tried tracing the error. In `tools/lib/provision.py`, it first catches the error by the exception `subprocess.CalledProcessError`. It then runs the script `scripts/lib/setup-apt-repo` which is the script for apt-get update. Here, if the zulip.list file has not changed, then  the command `apt-get update` is skipped. In my case ( broken package) it hadn't changed, and hence it skipped. So here, should we make changes directly in the exception  `subprocess.CalledProcessError` to run  `apt-get update`, or should we make changes in the script file?

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-29 16:39 UTC

@Rhea yeah, I think if it fails the first time, we should run `apt-get update` always, maybe just before it tries running `install_apt_deps` again.  Basically, we use caching to make the common case fast, but if we're in the slow case, we should make it works :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-29 16:39 UTC

(The reason we skip it is because `provision` takes like 10s to run if you're already provisioned, and `apt-get update` can take about that long)

**Rhea Parekh** · 2017-09-29 18:01 UTC

Okay! I'll add a PR soon for this!

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-09-29 18:08 UTC

awesome :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2017-10-16 18:20 UTC

@Shubham Dhama try editing your `/etc/hosts` to point `zulip.zulipdev.com` at 127.0.0.1.   That actually sounds like your machine isn't on the Internet / doesn't have DNS working properly.

Which one can work around how I described, by just hardcoding that config on your laptop.

**Tommy Ip** · 2017-11-06 11:27 UTC

`./tools/provision` is a script that updates dependencies, create python venvs, DBs. These are not coupled with the branch you are in

**Balaji** · 2017-11-06 11:29 UTC

I just updated my local environment with the upstream branch. And run that. Is this happened because of that?

**Tommy Ip** · 2017-11-06 11:30 UTC

Sometimes when we update dependencies or add new database migration we will change the provision version, so when you pull that change from upstream/master you will be prompt to do a provision

**Yashashvi Dave** · 2018-01-03 16:34 UTC

Because on master branch there are changes in database models.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2017-11-27 14:11 UTC

**Warn: do not use sudo to clone as that would result in file permission errors.**

There is some error with your public key config, which might take a separate debugging session, but for now use `git clone --config pull.rebase https://github.com/Abijith10/zulip.git`. Basically, use HTTPS instead of SSH for cloning. Since this can be changed later if you wish to, go ahead with HTTPS.

**Tommy Ip** · 2017-11-27 14:11 UTC

Do `git clone --config pull.rebase https://github.com/Abijith10/zulip.git` (github recommends HTTPS now anyway)

**Balaji** · 2017-11-27 14:15 UTC

In this [doc](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-vagrant.html#running-git-bash-as-an-administrator), it says you have to be an administrator and run the commands. So I thought Like that. Sorry for that.

**Tommy Ip** · 2017-11-27 14:16 UTC

Oh to do that you have to right click `git bash` and click `run as administrator`. @Abijith that should also work

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2017-11-27 14:18 UTC

@Balaji  That's for Windows. On linux, we usually have ext4 file systems and have granular permissions on files. Usually, a file created by the root/admin user won't be writable by the regular user so that would create other issues later.

**Rakin Uddin** · 2017-12-07 00:32 UTC

Hey @Alena Volkova , in regards to your original issue, I had the same where the 'zerver.lib.emoji' module could not be found.

It turns out that Vagrant has trouble syncing NFS folders on Mac OS X High Sierra (according to [this](https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/issues/8788) issue), so some folders are missing when you run `vagrant up`.
To fix it, I updated Mac OS X to the latest version (10.13.2) which fixes the NFS issue.

I also had to destroy my original vagrant VM with `vagrant destroy` and then re ran `vagrant up`. All the provisioning went successfully.

Hope that sheds some more insight on the issue.

**Alena Volkova** · 2017-12-07 12:16 UTC

@Rakin Uddin It worked! Thank you so much for sharing!

**Greg Price** · 2017-12-13 18:18 UTC

So it's giving an error as it tries to process a signature that uses this type:
> FuncKwargPair = Tuple[Callable[..., HttpResponse], Dict[str, Union[int, Iterable[Any]]]]

apparently because it's expecting that first argument to `Callable` to be a list.

I suspect this means we don't have a new enough `typing` -- that we're using the one from the stdlib instead of the latest.

**Greg Price** · 2017-12-13 18:18 UTC

We install a recent `typing`, but we must not have at this stage of provision.

**Greg Price** · 2017-12-13 18:19 UTC

So yeah, let's revert that change until we sort out the issue. Probably we need to reorder some steps in provision.

````
commit 17a6632c437b409f68e9469369c27c9edb36a388
Author: Greg Price <greg@zulipchat.com>
Date:   Wed Dec 13 10:20:11 2017 -0800

    zerver/views: Revert to Python 2 typing syntax for now (storage, streams).

    This reverts commit 620b2cd6e.

    Contributors setting up a new development environment were getting
    errors like this:
    ```
    ++ dirname tools/do-destroy-rebuild-database
    [...]
    + ./manage.py purge_queue --all
    Traceback (most recent call last):
    [...]
      File "/home/zulipdev/zulip/zproject/legacy_urls.py", line 3, in <module>
        import zerver.views.streams
      File "/home/zulipdev/zulip/zerver/views/streams.py", line 187, in <module>
        method_kwarg_pairs: List[FuncKwargPair]) -> HttpResponse:
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/typing.py", line 1025, in __getitem__
        tvars = _type_vars(params)
    [...]
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/typing.py", line 277, in _get_type_vars
        for t in types:
    TypeError: 'ellipsis' object is not iterable
    ```

    The issue appears to be that we're using the `typing` module from the
    3.5 stdlib, rather than the `typing=3.6.2` in our requirements files,
    and that doesn't understand the `Callable[..., HttpResponse]` that
    appears in the definition of `FuncKwargPair`.

    Revert for now to get provision working again; at least one person
    reports that reverting this sufficed.  We'll need to do more testing
    before putting this change back in.

**Vishnu KS** · 2018-02-08 19:28 UTC

@Tim Abbott Actually its a bit complicated than that. In good old days (ie vagrant version < 1.9.6) vagrant used to host their boxes in atlas.hashicorp.com.   All the boxes have a file called `metadata_url` which caches the URL from where it downloaded the box. So vagrant uses `metadata_url` for checking whether the box should be updated or not. When vagrant downloads a new box it tries to get it from `Vagrant::DEFAULT_SERVER_URL`. The value of `Vagrant::DEFAULT_SERVER_URL` was of course  atlas.hashicorp.com.

One day they had this idea to host the boxes in vagrantcloud.com instead of atlas.hashicorp.com. Since this will break all the older vagrant versions they decided to add a temporary redirect from  atlas.hashicorp.com  -> vagrantcloud.com.  In 1.9.6 they updated the code to change the `Vagrant::DEFAULT_SERVER_URL` to  vagrantcloud.com. So when the users download a new box it would be fetched from vagrantcloud.com instead of atlas.hashicorp.com. As far the boxes downloaded from old vagrant versions are concerned they still check for updates from atlas.hashicorp.com as that is the value of metadata_url. It would work fine as there is a redirect from  atlas.hashicorp.com -> vagrantcloud.com.

A few days back hell broke loose. They decided to remove the  atlas.hashicorp.com  -> vagrantcloud.com redirect. So now all the vagrant versions < 1.9.6 can't download new boxes and update old boxes as they have the value of `metadata_url` and  `Vagrant::DEFAULT_SERVER_URL` as atlas.hashicorp.com. The users who have vagrant >= `1.9.6` installed can download new boxes the value of `Vagrant::DEFAULT_SERVER_URL` is vagrantcloud.com . But if they have boxes which were download using a vagrant version < 1.9.6 they can't update them as cached the metadata_url of the boxes have the value atlas.hashicorp.com.

So we have to recommend all new contributors to install a vagrant version >= 1.9.6. Alternatively, we can ask them to use `1.8.6` but we have to make a slight modification in Vagrantfile. We have to add this line. `Vagrant::DEFAULT_SERVER_URL.replace('https://vagrantcloud.com')`

Our current developers who are using vagrant versions < 1.9.6 have to replace the value of `meta_data` URL manually if they want to check for new updates. But since the updates are not necessary I guess this can be probably skipped. :)

## Issue with mypy / Travis CI

*2017-12-28 to 2017-12-28 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Issue.20with.20mypy.20.2F.20Travis.20CI/with/413762)*

**Andy Perez** · 2017-12-28 15:27 UTC

Hey!  I was hoping someone could help me diagnose what's going on in this Travis CI build that ends in an error
https://travis-ci.org/PentaHiggs/zulip/jobs/322569899
Only the last python 3.5 test fails; it fails because it cannot import `Deque` from `typing` in `zerver/lib/bugdown/__init__.py`.  This isn't an issue in any of the other tests, nor of the test on my vagrant dev environment.  Why is it a problem here?
mypy was updated to support the `Deque`container as a type not that long ago, could it be possible that the version number of mypy installed for that test is different than the one installed in the vagrant dev environment / on python 3.4 ?

It's not too important to figure out, I can always make mypy ignore a few lines instead.  It would be nice to figure out what's going on, though.

**Andy Perez** · 2017-12-28 16:29 UTC

Nevermind, I figured it out, I think.  I always get rather confused by how provisioning and dependencies work in this project, but I believe what happened is that

* We install the `typing` module in python 3.4, which is a backport from a python version > 3.6
* Deque support was added in python 3.5.4
* In python 3.4, everything is fine because we're using the backported module, there is no native `typing` module in the language yet.
* The `typing` module is natively part of  python in python 3.5
* The `typing` backport is only for python versions < 3.5, according to pypi, so pip doesn't touch the native module at all.
* Deque support was added to it in python 3.5.4, we use python 3.5.3, so it's not there and I get an error.

https://pypi.python.org/pypi/typing-extensions contains a backport of future typing stuff to python versions 3.5/3.6, so it could possibly fix things (Or possibly not since it assumes you're using the latest python 3.5 version)

It really does seem like the solution here is to give up on what I want and just tell mypy to ignore a few lines after all, because to make this work both on python 3.5.3 and any other python version < 3.5 or >= 3.5.4 simultaneously is a pain.  Does anyone disagree?

And uh, I think this is the wrong stream for this, although it might be tangentially related.  Sorry about that!

**Andy Perez** · 2017-12-28 17:11 UTC

And yes, Python 3.5 currently aliases to 3.5.3 instead of the newer 3.5.4 on Travis-CI.  If we specify `python=3.5.4` or `python=3.5-dev` in the travis configuration file then there is no trouble at all.  Is it okay to change to one of those two, or is there reason to test whether zulip works specifically on 3.5.3

**Steve Howell** · 2017-12-28 20:45 UTC

I think we should just tell mypy to ignore those lines for now.

**Andy Perez** · 2017-12-28 20:49 UTC

Yes, you're right.  That's what I ended up doing in the end.  Python 3.5.4 is a rather recent bugfix release for the 3.5 line anyway, 3.5 will most likely alias to it eventually given time, it's better to just not mess with it and move on :stuck_out_tongue:

@Yuki I just wanted to give a quick response--sometimes we run into issues like yours, and the best solution is to do essentially what you did.  Our provision process is designed to be idempotent, so particularly for temporary outages, you can sometimes just run the provision successfully after some time has passed.

**Eeshan Garg** · 2018-01-19 03:35 UTC

Okay, so I have been trying to track this down for the past hour-ish. I haven't been able to reproduce it. Here's what I found:
* `generate_zulip_bots_static_files` is the only setup script that seems to want to remove an entire directory and it's contents.
* The `generated` directory has the permissions `drwxr-xr-x`.
* The `generated/bots/` directory has the permissions `drwxrwxr-x`.
* A directory such as `generated/bots/<bot_name>/` has the permissions `drwxrwxr-x`.
* A `generated/bots/<bot_name>/doc.md` file has the permissions `-rw-rw-r--`.

My guess is that the reason the script can't delete `doc.md` is because the parent directory of `bots/`, i.e., the `generated/` directory doesn't give write access to the users in the same group as the file owner's. Or is it the `doc.md` file's permissions here? Isn't it supposed to be that in order to delete a directory or file, the user must have write access to the parent directory of the the directory/file to be removed?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-01-19 22:50 UTC

In UNIX, user accounts own files; scripts (which from the perspective of the filesystem are just files) do not.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-01-19 22:50 UTC

If I had to guess, this is some sort of user ID mismatch issue with Vagrant.

**Eeshan Garg** · 2018-01-19 22:51 UTC

Okay, that makes sense about file ownership. Well then, it can't possibly be the script's fault, all it does is copy over some files, which a few other scripts do all the time.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-01-19 23:08 UTC

I should clarify that I also hypothesize that `./tools/setup/generate_zulip_bots_static_files` is not the source of the issue here, it's the victim.  But I think @Eeshan Garg may still be the best person to debug this.  Another data point here is that I've re-provisioned a couple times since this has been reported, and I haven't encountered the issue myself, which makes me a little suspicious that the problem is being aggravated by users doing "funny things."  Which isn't their fault--just makes it hard to repro and fix.

The tooling is not designed to support that operation, since in production, the `zulip` user is the owner of various files, whereas in development, it's whatever user account you're logged in as.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2018-02-22 03:37 UTC

@Andrea Kao , we recently updated our vagrant version form 1.8.6 to 2.0.2 in our docs file.(while debugging for ubuntu)
Can you try running with vagrant version 1.8.6?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-02-22 05:04 UTC

@Andrea Kao that looks like a filesystem problem, where some files that are present in the host are not showing up in the guest; basically an OSX NFS bug.  I would try rebooting the guest (`vagrant reload`) and see if that fixes it.

**Konstantin Novokreshchenov** · 2018-02-23 10:59 UTC

@Andrea Kao I had the same issue. I tried to install different versions of vagrant/virtualbox but problem hadn't disappeared. After googling I found this issue: https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/issues/8788. It seems to be a bug in MacOS High Sierra. What is your version of macOS? Try to update to latest version 10.13.3. I had version 10.13.1 when error was observed. After updating to 10.13.3 problem disappeared and zulip environment setup works fine!

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-02-23 16:45 UTC

Interesting; @Konstantin Novokreshchenov can you add a note about this to the MacOS requirements section of our documentation (basically that High Sierra before 10.13.3 has a filesystem bug that causes problems)?  It'd be good to help future users avoid this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-02-23 16:46 UTC

Also @Brock Whittaker FYI, since I know you've run into similar problems in the past.

**Konstantin Novokreshchenov** · 2018-02-24 18:28 UTC

@Tim Abbott Sure! Should I create separate issue about it? Or should I make only regular PR with descriptive name?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-02-24 21:48 UTC

@Konstantin Novokreshchenov I think just a PR is fine for a documentation tweak like this.

**Konstantin Novokreshchenov** · 2018-02-25 10:52 UTC

@Tim Abbott Added PR https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/8508 with description of such error

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-02-25 17:15 UTC

Great, thanks :)

**Johnny Yang** · 2018-04-12 10:49 UTC

Hi all,

```
    default: error An unexpected error occurred: "EACCES: permission denied, scandir '/home/vagrant/.config/yarn/link'".
    default: info If you think this is a bug, please open a bug report with the information provided in "/srv/zulip-npm-cache/85c2ac3c8aab9f4c07e779f3c1e4082a81980ccd/yarn-error.log".
    default: info Visit https://yarnpkg.com/en/docs/cli/install for documentation about this command.
    default:
    default: Error running a subcommand of ./lib/provision.py: /srv/zulip/scripts/lib/cd_exec /srv/zulip-npm-cache/85c2ac3c8aab9f4c07e779f3c1e4082a81980ccd /srv/zulip-yarn/bin/yarn install --non-interactive --prefer-offline
    default: Actual error output for the subcommand is just above this.
```
I'm on Mac 10.13.4 (High Sierra). A copy of my provision log has been attached. Thanks again. [provision.log](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/f5/H8AJTx3xeJBmdQx9mqsLMHf0/provision.log)

**Steve Howell** · 2018-04-12 10:55 UTC

@Johnny Yang I'm not sure, but this appears to be a symptom that you may have run a command as root before encountering this error that led to `/home/vagrant/.config/yarn/link` having the wrong permissions for a new user.

**Johnny Yang** · 2018-04-12 10:59 UTC

Hi @Steve Howell , thanks for the quick reply. I did try using 'sudo' while troubleshooting the issue, but the error came up the first time I ran vagrant up/provision without sudo.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-04-12 11:06 UTC

That would explain it, I think.  When you ran as `sudo`, even though you weren't fully successful, you created the directory in question with `root` permissions.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-04-12 11:06 UTC

And now your normal user can't access those files.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-04-12 11:08 UTC

There are a couple ways to remedy this, none of them perfect:
* use `sudo chown` to fix directory permissions as you see errors like this
* remove the affected hidden directories (which assumes they will get re-created properly, which is mostly a valid assumption, but not a guarantee)
* just wipe your zulip directory clean and start over

**Steve Howell** · 2018-04-12 11:09 UTC

I recommend the wipe-clean-and-start-over approach.  It's a bit more time consuming at first, but it will likely prevent you from going down a rabbit hole of debugging.

**Johnny Yang** · 2018-04-12 11:15 UTC

Okay, I'll do that then. Thanks.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-04-12 11:15 UTC

Good luck!

But when I run `vagrant up`inside the zulip repo, I get `There was an error executing ["sudo", "/usr/local/bin/vagrant-lxc-wrapper", "lxc-start", "-d", "--name", "zulip_default_1523910521120_52265"]`

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-04-16 21:33 UTC

@Dusty Phillips hello!  It's not a known issue, but we also don't have any long-term community members who use Fedora AFAIK.  We don't integrate with LXC beyond the basic Vagrant configuration, though, so I don't think any Zulip expertise should be required to debug.

I agree the log doesn't have a smoking gun.  It looks like you're getting an error that's some sort of Vagrant+LXC+Fedora 27 interaction (i.e., it's not getting to any of our code).  So I'd try Googling a bit to debug; I bet someone else has run into this before (I'm guessing it's something in the general space of permissions).

**Colin Panisset** · 2018-04-18 05:01 UTC

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2018-05-18 13:41 UTC

On Vagrant 2.0.2 (the recommended one) on 18.04 I got this error:

```
$ vagrant plugin install vagrant-lxc
Installing the 'vagrant-lxc' plugin. This can take a few minutes...
Bundler, the underlying system Vagrant uses to install plugins,
reported an error. The error is shown below. These errors are usually
caused by misconfigured plugin installations or transient network
issues. The error from Bundler is:

conflicting dependencies fog-core (~> 1.43.0) and fog-core (= 1.45.0)
  Activated fog-core-1.45.0
  which does not match conflicting dependency (~> 1.43.0)

  Conflicting dependency chains:
    fog-core (= 1.45.0), 1.45.0 activated

  versus:
    vagrant-libvirt (> 0), 0.0.41 activated, depends on
    fog-core (~> 1.43.0)
```

According to https://github.com/dotless-de/vagrant-vbguest/issues/292 this is fixed in 2.0.3. Should we update our docs regarding this?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2018-05-18 13:45 UTC

There is also v2.1.1 available in case we are upgrading.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-05-18 21:05 UTC

@Rohitt Vashishtha yeah, I think it's totally reasonable to upgrade the version we recommend.  The main reason we recommend a fixed version is just to make sure we've tested the version we're recommending ourselves; Vagrant has done a few broken releases in the past.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2018-05-22 19:08 UTC

On continued usage, I think there might be some issues to resolve. If I do `vagrant halt` and then `vagrant up` again without rebooting, I get this:

```
$ vagrant up
Bringing machine 'default' up with 'lxc' provider...
==> default: Checking if box 'fgrehm/trusty64-lxc' is up to date...
Vagrant cannot forward the specified ports on this VM, since they
would collide with some other application that is already listening
on these ports. The forwarded port to 9991 is already in use
on the host machine.

To fix this, modify your current project's Vagrantfile to use another
port. Example, where '1234' would be replaced by a unique host port:

  config.vm.network :forwarded_port, guest: 9991, host: 1234

Sometimes, Vagrant will attempt to auto-correct this for you. In this
case, Vagrant was unable to. This is usually because the guest machine
is in a state which doesn't allow modifying port forwarding. You could
try 'vagrant reload' (equivalent of running a halt followed by an up)
so vagrant can attempt to auto-correct this upon booting. Be warned
that any unsaved work might be lost.
```

There seems to be a process called `redir` that is listening on the ports that we need vagrant to to listen to (9991 and 9994). Killing it and then running `vagrant up` works as expected.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-05-22 20:48 UTC

Hmm, see whether a newer version fixes that?  Definitely looks like basically `vagrant halt` not shutting down the `redir` proxy properly.

## dev environment over https?

*2018-11-01 to 2018-11-01 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/dev.20environment.20over.20https.3F/with/657457)*

**Gavagai** · 2018-11-01 15:35 UTC

Is there a simple way to get the vagrant dev environment to serve over https? I'm trying to expand the OAuth functionality, and many identity providers require https endpoints.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-11-01 17:42 UTC

@Gavagai hmm, good question.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-11-01 17:43 UTC

I don't think there's a simple way to do that directly, but you could run a webserver like `nginx` and configure it to reverse-proxy to your Zulip development environment.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-11-01 17:44 UTC

https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/deployment.html#putting-the-zulip-application-behind-a-reverse-proxy might be helpful if you haven't done that sort of thing before; I think a good goal would be to write a simple `nginx` configuration file that can be used for this purpose and check it in + document it, so nobody else has to figure this out.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-11 18:04 UTC

@FtoL check out https://docs.docker.com/network/proxy/ -- I think it addresses your question on how to set proxy variables.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-11 18:04 UTC

If that works for you, we can add a link to the Docker image documentation so others can find it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-11 18:04 UTC

(I think you should just need to set `HTTP_PROXY` and friends, but not sure as I don't have a convenient way to test)

**FtoL** · 2019-01-15 06:14 UTC

@Tim Abbott 
> check out https://docs.docker.com/network/proxy/ -- I think it addresses your question on how to set proxy variables.
 This proxy settings are for the docker host. Has nothing to do with my issue ;) 

There a differences between a proxy setting for the docker host and the containers. The settings for the host will be persistant. I am able to pull images afterwards for example.
The settings within a new container form a new image does not have any ENV settings so it is not able to communicate with the outside world (internet). Therefore I have recommended to configure the files "/etc/environment" ,  "/etc/wgetrc" and "/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/proxy.conf". If you don't the zulip setup and config will not work properly cause the containers are not abel to talk to an "apt update" server for example. The issue is that if you want to use wget within a new container for example if you run the "setup-certbot" script, it does not work cause of no proxy is configured.
To make this setting persistant in every new zulip container a change of the dockerfile is neccessary. Do you know what I mean?

## Vagrant suspend

*2019-05-03 to 2019-05-03 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Vagrant.20suspend/with/738887)*

**Vinit Singh** · 2019-05-03 16:15 UTC

The `vagrant suspend` command used to work on my system when I had windows. About a month ago I made the switch to Ubuntu and it doesn't seem to work anymore.  Although `vagrant halt` does the job in my case, is there a reason suspend doesn't work? Or did I mess something up with my dev env setup?

This is what I get when I run the command
```bash
vinit@vinit-Aspire-V3-574G ~/Zulip/zulip (max_upload) $ vagrant suspend
Vagrant attempted to call the action 'suspend' on the provider
'LXC (zulip_default_1554902190439_73709)', but this provider doesn't support this action. This
is probably a bug in either the provider or the plugin calling this
action, and should be reported.
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-03 21:05 UTC

@Vinit Singh yeah, so this relates to a different Vagrant guest technology.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-03 21:06 UTC

With a VM, you can "suspend" it (the same thing as closing your laptop does to stop it while keeping its full state); this saves the time that it would otherwise take the kernel to boot up.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-03 21:06 UTC

With the container system (like Docker or the LXC used by Vagrant here), you can't do that, because the guest is sharing the kernel with the host OS.

**Vinit Singh** · 2019-05-03 21:08 UTC

Ah, okay. That makes sense. Thank you explaining that :smile:

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-06-30 06:55 UTC

I messed around with this for a bit the other night and found a simple reproduction:
* Bump provision
* `rm -r srv/zulip-npm-cache`
* Disconnect from network
* `tools/provision`
* Hangs on yarn reattempt, during the ~60s timeout, reconnect to network.
* Throws the above error

It looks like `zulip_tools.py` is already catching the `CalledProcessError` and adding that 
`Error running a subcommand of ...` message.  What I found could also be a source of confusion is that `yarn` will keep making reattempts after a 60s timeout with a flaky internet connection.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-07-01 19:44 UTC

Opened #12688

One thing I'd like to note: I couldn't see a tried and true way to check if the user is running in Vagrant.  The current approach just greps for existence of the `vagrant` user.  I added a comment for details.

After doing some reading, a more solid approach would be to `touch` a reference file in the following block at the end of the `Vagrantfile`:
```ruby
 config.vm.provision "shell",
```
And then `or`-ing the existence of that file in the conditional.  Not sure if that's entirely necessary, but it would be more reliable.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-01 22:37 UTC

We can’t rely on anyone rerunning the `config.vm.provision` block—that doesn’t happen except on the first `vagrant up` or an explicit `vagrant up --provision`.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-07-01 22:50 UTC

Right, I was thinking  of a way to eventually transition to a more reliable check. So it would be something like:
```python
if subprocess.check_call(['grep', '...']) or os.path.isfile(/path/is_vagrant)
```
But what you mentioned is where my skepticism stems from.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-07-01 22:51 UTC

(or if there is a better way all together to check if one is running in vagrant)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-01 22:55 UTC

We can’t transition to a more reliable check for a condition that only existed before the transition began. If we add an `is_vagrant` file, anyone who has it will already not be running trusty.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-01 22:56 UTC

I suggested `os.path.exists('/home/vagrant')` on the PR.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-07-01 22:59 UTC

Ahh right, of course. Just saw that, thanks!

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-01 23:01 UTC

(If it comes up again, the Pythonic way to literally check whether a user exists would be `pwd.getpwnam('vagrant')`, catching `KeyError`. But I don’t think that would happen without `/home/vagrant` existing, for our purposes.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-01 05:58 UTC

@Anders Kaseorg can you help investigate this precedence issue on macOS?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-01 05:58 UTC

@Tyler Thrailkill `vagrant up --provider=virtualbox` should work for forcing the provider; sounds like there's an auto-detection bug here

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-01 06:12 UTC

Well the detection is behaving as designed: Docker if available, else VirtualBox. Certainly Vagrant upstream wouldn’t want a patch that unilaterally blacklists Docker for Mac, since it works fine for many things, and might even work fine for us if we investigated the issue.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-01 06:14 UTC

Probably that issue is [this one](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43097341/docker-on-macosx-does-not-translate-file-ownership-correctly-in-volumes).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-01 06:18 UTC

If we can’t get it to work, we could try to add some weird conditional logic to Vagrantfile, but probably the right answer is to document `vagrant up --provider=virtualbox` and move on.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-01 06:19 UTC

(You should only need to do it once.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-03 21:36 UTC

@Anders Kaseorg that's a reasonable solution; we'll need to do a bit of refactoring because `vagrant up` is currently part of the shared content between different platforms, but that's fine.

## Xenial and Bionic Boxes

*2019-07-20 to 2019-07-22 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Xenial.20and.20Bionic.20Boxes/with/770620)*

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-07-20 17:34 UTC

Right now, my development environment is  Vagrant + Ubuntu Bionic (with Docker) and my host OS is Ubuntu Bionic as well. For the most part my current Vagrant dev environment is just great, but sometimes, I need to locally test things out using a configuration that's similar to the Xenial box that we run our CircleCI tests on. So is there a way to be able to set up a Xenial dev environment alongside my Bionic one using a simple procedure? The [docs](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-vagrant.html) currently don't have much info on this and I currently have a limited knowledge of Vagrant.

Right now I'm thinking about creating a VirtualBox with Ubuntu Xenial Server and then following the [advanced development environment setup guide](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/overview.html). But this is nowhere near as convenient as the Vagrant dev environment, so I'm pretty sure that there's a better way.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-21 21:42 UTC

@Hemanth V. Alluri you generally shouldn't need to run a Xenial box outside CI; it's rare that there are different results on different platforms (as opposed to simply nondeterministic results that happen to fail on one or the other).  That said, I'm pretty sure it should be possible to patch our `Vagrantfile` to support a Xenial container, and we ideally would offer that as an option.  @Anders Kaseorg do you know what we need to do for this?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-21 21:46 UTC

Probably a bit more fighting with docker-systemctl-replacement. I didn’t get it to work last time I tried but that was before the last docker-systemctl-replacement upgrade, so maybe it works better now.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-21 21:49 UTC

The starting point would be
```diff
--- a/tools/setup/dev-vagrant-docker/Dockerfile
+++ b/tools/setup/dev-vagrant-docker/Dockerfile
@@ -1 +1 @@
-FROM ubuntu:18.04
+FROM ubuntu:16.04
@@ -15 +15 @@ RUN echo locales locales/default_environment_locale select en_US.UTF-8 | debconf
-    && printf 'y\n\n' | unminimize \
+    && apt-get update \
@@ -41 +41 @@ RUN \
-    && ln -ns /lib/systemd/system/postgresql@.service /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/postgresql@10-main.service \
+    && ln -ns /lib/systemd/system/postgresql@.service /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/postgresql@9.5-main.service \
```
which I’ll try out now.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-21 22:13 UTC

Well it works on first boot, but on subsequent reboots you’ll need to manually start Postgres using the non-systemd initscript (`/etc/init.d/postgresql start`). Needs some work before we can add this as a supported option, but maybe that’s good enough for your testing.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-17 16:15 UTC

Huh, `libpcre3-dev` is not one of our declared dependencies; I wonder if it's a recursive dependency?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-17 16:15 UTC

Looks like `uwsgi` is what was failing to install.  I don't have time to investigate this morning but that should be enough to investigate.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-17 16:16 UTC

https://uwsgi-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Install.html does not seem to think you need that package, hmm.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-12-17 16:26 UTC

uWSGI detects the presence of PCRE at build time using the `pcre-config` command. The only way you could have seen that error is if it found `pcre-config` but did not find the corresponding headers. Perhaps you had previously installed a version of this command without the headers, or removed the headers without removing the command, or one of them was in a nonstandard path?

## experimental docker setup

*2019-08-08 to 2019-08-20 · 64 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/experimental.20docker.20setup/with/777574)*

**David Rosa** · 2019-08-08 17:15 UTC

I ran into a lot of issues trying to get Vagrant with Docker to work on macOS. It works with VirtualBox, but it seems kind of slow and resource-heavy. I wanted to see if I could get the Zulip development environment up and running with docker only. I got it working last night!

**David Rosa** · 2019-08-08 17:16 UTC

So here's an alternative setup to what's described in [ReadTheDocs/development/overview](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/overview.html). I would like to make a PR if others find it useful too. You can have a look at the following commit for more details:
https://github.com/drrosa/zulip/commit/d901e800586e2974c0f27b290b21bef6cd8d0ed7

 I've only tried it on macOS Mojave, but it should also work on Docker supported Linux platforms, and hopefully on Windows too.

**David Rosa** · 2019-08-08 17:19 UTC

The docker image is based on [phusion/baseimage-docker](https://github.com/phusion/baseimage-docker): "A minimal Ubuntu base image modified for Docker-friendliness."

Estimated setup time is about ~20 mins when using a high-speed internet connection. Here are the instructions if anyone wants to give it a try:

**David Rosa** · 2019-08-08 17:28 UTC

**0. Install Docker**
https://docs.docker.com/install/#supported-platforms

**1.  Get Zulip Code**

```
mkdir zulipdev-docker && cd zulipdev-docker
git clone https://github.com/drrosa/zulip.git
cd zulip
git checkout provision-docker
```

**2. Copy the Dockerfile into the working directory and build the docker image**
```
cp tools/setup/dev-docker/Dockerfile ..
cd ..
time docker build -t zulip-dev .
```

3. **Run container, Clone Zulip code, Provision docker volumes, and run the Zulip dev server** 

`docker run --name=zulip-dev --rm -it -p 9991:9991 -v zulip-home-vol:/home/zulipdev -v zulip-srv-vol:/srv -v zulip-vol:/mnt/zulip zulip-dev`
```
git clone --config pull.rebase https://github.com/YOURUSERNAME/zulip.git /mnt/zulip
git remote add -f upstream https://github.com/zulip/zulip.git
git remote add -f drrosa https://github.com/drrosa/zulip.git
git checkout drrosa/provision-docker
```

```
time ./tools/provision
source /srv/zulip-py3-venv/bin/activate
./tools/run-dev.py
```

Now open up your browser and go to http://0.0.0.0:9991

## unmask docker

*2019-09-21 to 2019-09-22 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/unmask.20docker/with/787829)*

**Yash RE** · 2019-09-21 05:24 UTC

I did a fresh install of docker and got this error:
```
re@re:~$ sudo systemctl enable docker
Synchronizing state of docker.service with SysV service script with /lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install.
Executing: /lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install enable docker
Failed to enable unit: Unit file /etc/systemd/system/docker.service is masked.
```

I followed https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37227349/unable-to-start-docker-service-in-ubuntu-16-04 and this worked:
```
> sudo systemctl unmask docker.service
> sudo systemctl unmask docker.socket
> sudo systemctl enable docker
> sudo systemctl start docker.service
```

Should we add this to the docs?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-21 13:30 UTC

Seems plausible; @Anders Kaseorg do you think we should recommend running that unconditionally in our Docker install docs block?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-21 20:05 UTC

I’d like to hear more about this happened. What version of Ubuntu, and how did you install Docker (`apt install docker.io`, `snap install docker`, or something involving docker.com)?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-21 21:02 UTC

Oh, I have a theory about what might cause this:
1. On Ubuntu 16.04, `apt-get install docker.io`
2. `apt-get remove docker.io` (without purging it)
3. Upgrade to Ubuntu 18.04
4. `apt-get install docker.io`

Will attempt to test this. @Yash RE does that sound like what might have happened?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-21 22:25 UTC

Filed [LP #1844894](https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/docker.io/+bug/1844894).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-21 23:09 UTC

Opened #13210.

**Yash RE** · 2019-09-22 04:23 UTC

That's very close. I didn't change Ubuntu versions though, this was a clean 18.04, at some point I had installed some version of docker (with some version of containerd) and then I installed docker as our docs suggest, but without purging anything apart from containerd.

**Mehant Kumar** · 2021-04-07 18:35 UTC

I figured it out... I deleted ```/var/lib/docker```, restarted docker and again installed the container image using ```vagrant up --provider=docker```
I actually messed with the ```/var/lib/docker``` dir permissions few days back.
Thanks :smile:

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-07 18:59 UTC

OK; probably given that context, there's probably not a change we should make for our troubleshooting guide/tooling, unless we think other folks are likely to have manually changed permissions of `/var/lib/docker`.

**Ray Kraesig** · 2020-01-10 18:19 UTC

@Prajneya Kumar: Sounds like `vagrant` just isn't in your `$PATH` for some reason. Maybe try the following?

* Assuming you're in Bash, `hash -r`. (It [shouldn't be necessary](https://superuser.com/q/999439), but it's easy to try.)
* Failing that, the output of `which vagrant` and/or `echo $PATH` might be illuminating.
* Failing *that*,  `dpkg -L vagrant` should list all the files installed by the `vagrant` package. You may need to manually compare that with `$PATH`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-01-23 01:28 UTC

For those who are curious, we run multiple servers on the ports 9991, 9992, 9993, etc., and `run-dev.py` itself is a proxy running on port 9991 that directs traffic to the relevant service.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-01-23 01:29 UTC

Each service prints its own output on startup about what port its starting up on, but the Vagrant environment only exposes port 9991 externally, since anything accessing Zulip should just be using that port (and relying on the proxy).

## Git: Conflicts in git rebase

*2020-02-11 to 2020-02-11 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Git.3A.20Conflicts.20in.20git.20rebase/with/816036)*

**Madhav** · 2020-02-11 15:20 UTC

I am getting conflicts every time i try to do git rebase, even after manually solving the conflicts. I did use git pull a few times, and later on I found out from the documentation that I shouldn't have used it. Is it because of that?
How can I fix this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-11 20:18 UTC

@Madhav I'd recommend using a graphical viewer to see what's happening in your Git repository.  But yes, a common consequence of using `git pull --merge` (the default if you didn't follow our instructions to clone the repository with the setting to default to `git pull --rebase`) is that you can end up with merge commits and copies of commits in master that may merge conflict when you try to rebase them.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-04 22:46 UTC

@Divyanshu Agrawal `du -shc` is a helpful tool for figuring out what is consuming space.  I'd start with looking under `/srv`.  

I certainly wouldn't expect our development environment to require 10GB.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-03-04 22:50 UTC

Note that some amount of your free space (default 5%) is reserved for use by the `root` user, which is why `df` only shows `606M` free. Probably all the non-reserved space was used at the time of that error.

**Divyanshu Agrawal** · 2020-03-05 06:01 UTC

Thanks @Tim Abbott @Anders Kaseorg ! I have one question -  Isn't the error due to the container running out of space? And , I think, since the container is installed in my /home partition, which has a lot of empty space, there shouldn't be a lack of space issue?

What could be causing the using up of space in the root (/) partition?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-03-05 06:04 UTC

The container is managed by Docker. It’s probably somewhere in `/var/lib/docker`, depending on how you installed Docker.

**Divyanshu Agrawal** · 2020-03-05 07:43 UTC

Fixed, thanks a lot for your help!

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-03-23 20:19 UTC

You can check with `env | grep ^LC` inside and outside the droplet.

**Yash RE** · 2020-03-23 20:33 UTC

I did explicitly set `LC_ALL=C` on my local system because I wanted to fix `key-mon`.
I didn't expect that to effect the droplet though? Would it change if I ssh from a different system?

**Yash RE** · 2020-03-23 20:35 UTC

(`LC_ALL=C` is actually in my local `~/.bashrc`, I put it there)

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-23 20:37 UTC

Locale environment variables are passed through SSH.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-23 20:37 UTC

So that is an expected consequence of what you did on your local system.

**Yash RE** · 2020-03-23 20:43 UTC

Oooh. Ok then, that makes sense. (thanks Anders!)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-03-23 20:47 UTC

Yeah setting `LC_ALL` is likely to break many applications in unexpected ways, since its purpose is to override all the other locale settings, and the `C` locale does not support Unicode.

**Ray Kraesig** · 2020-03-23 20:54 UTC

When you *do* need a `C`-like locale, you usually want `C.UTF-8` instead.

**Ray Kraesig** · 2020-03-23 20:54 UTC

(Or at least, that's what I use on my home system.)

I'll fix `provision` to handle this correctly; I think the development history is that we moved the `apt-get update` out of `provision` and into `setup-apt-repo`, but then we made the `setup-apt-repo` conditional as that was correct in production, but didn't add an `apt update` in development.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-23 20:47 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-23 21:04 UTC

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> Moving the `apt-get update` before `setup-apt-repo` would be strictly more efficient.
Oh?  I would have thought we'd do `apt-get update` the same number of times either way.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-23 21:05 UTC

The reason I was thinking it should go after is in case `setup-apt-repo` removes any sources that, say, no longer exist, the `apt-get update` might fail.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-03-23 21:08 UTC

With `apt-get update` before `setup-apt-repo`, we might get to skip the `apt-get update` that `setup-apt-repo` does if it fails to install the `pre_setup_deps`.

Which I think is typical on initial provision.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-23 21:17 UTC

**Divyanshu Agrawal** · 2020-04-14 18:48 UTC

@Chris Bobbe As far as I recall:
Originally, I had two partitions: / (root) for my filesystem root and /home for user directories. Since my root partition was almost filled up, I was running out of space while provisioning. So I created a new partiton out of my home partition and mounted it as /usr and moved the contents of the original /usr folder to this new (large, empty) parition. Since docker and the dependencies install to /usr, I had pleny of space now, and the lack of space issue got fixed.

**Divyanshu Agrawal** · 2020-04-14 18:50 UTC

Awesome! Looks like you solved the lack of space issue!

## email IDs?

*2020-05-01 to 2020-05-01 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/email.20IDs.3F/with/866104)*

**cypherpunks** · 2020-05-01 01:09 UTC

here on CZO when i narrow to "view messages sent" from a user, the search query is their actual email address. but on my instance i recently setup and did a slack import on, users are identified as userN@examplecom (where example.com is the subdomain of my zulip instance, and N is some small number, presumably sequential). I thought maybe this was just for accounts imported from slack, but after inviting and adding a guest user i see it is the case for them too.

Stranger still, in the Manage Organization table of users, I see an email column with everyone's real email address - but when i click to modify a user, the window that appears shows their bogus userN@example.com type of address!

What is going on here?

**cypherpunks** · 2020-05-01 01:12 UTC

(also - sorry i just realized this is the wrong stream for this (though i'm not sure what the right one is))

**Vaibhav Raj Singh** · 2020-05-01 08:51 UTC

(replying to cypherpunks)
> (also - sorry i just realized this is the wrong stream for this (though i'm not sure what the right one is))
#**production help** is usually apt for dropping of queries regarding prod.

**Dinesh Ch** · 2020-05-01 10:53 UTC

It is most probably because of email visibility is only set to admins. We have two sorts of emails, `delivery_email` and `email` where `delivery_email` is used to send email notifications, and for all other purposes in a realm `email`which is usually in form of userN@example.com is used.
This comment I found in `models.py` might help:
```
    # For historical reasons, Zulip has two email fields.  The
    # `delivery_email` field is the user's email address, where all
    # email notifications will be sent, and is used for all
    # authentication use cases.
    #
    # The `email` field is the same as delivery_email in organizations
    # with EMAIL_ADDRESS_VISIBILITY_EVERYONE.  For other
    # organizations, it will be a unique value of the form
    # user1234@example.com.  This field exists for backwards
    # compatibility in Zulip APIs where users are referred to by their
    # email address, not their ID; it should be used in all API use cases.
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-01 18:19 UTC

@cypherpunks yeah, this is consistent with the current behavior for the setting limiting access to real email addresses to organization administrators.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-01 18:19 UTC

Because an "email" field is still used in a few places in the API in that case, we use fake the emails for that purpose.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-01 18:19 UTC

The planend solution is to stop showing email addresses (as opposed to user pills) in the search area; but we can't do that without some restructuring.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-01 18:20 UTC

If you chose the setting that allows it, organization administrators see email addresses in contexts that involve managing users.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-01 18:21 UTC

We thought the feature to not have email addresses be widely shared important enough that we wanted to ship it even before finishing the API/UI migrations that would not show an "email" field, hence the fake email addresses that appear in some places.

## Vagrant up not starting

*2020-05-19 to 2020-05-22 · 41 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Vagrant.20up.20not.20starting/with/881247)*

**Hendrik Visage** · 2020-05-19 07:19 UTC

(HAd it before in #**tools** Vagrant):

I just last night tested MAIN zulip branch with vagrant on MacOS (10.14.6, Vagrant 2.2.9, VirtualBox 6.1.8)

It just, doesn't start, stuck on the booting of that VM (and it "stuck" VBox Manager too ;(). seems that this line in VagrantFile is the guilty:
```
123     vb.customize [ "modifyvm", :id, "--uartmode1", "disconnected" ]
```
Commenting it out, and the VM starts and gets configured

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-19 17:07 UTC

@Hendrik Visage interesting, thanks for the report.  857c16d52d91845c3f69e8d87d952ddc806a259e seems to be what introduced that line; @Wyatt Hoodes do you remember more context on this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-19 17:08 UTC

It seems plausible that the upstream `bionic` box fixed their bug and that's why we should remove this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-19 17:08 UTC

I don't have a convenient macOS environment to test personally.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 17:17 UTC

Huh yeah, I can look into that a little later today.  Though it seems strange to me that this line would interfere with the booting process as it just overrides the base box writing out a log file.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 17:19 UTC

But I’ll certainly look into it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-19 18:18 UTC

I doubt changing the `uartmode1` on the VM just modifies logging.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 19:58 UTC

Ahh, you're right. I was thinking about Docker, sorry. I think I found some [reasoning](https://github.com/Berkeley-CS162/vagrant/blob/f506d21529b130f63c68fb830ebafdb07dc44cd2/Vagrantfile#L26)
The comment from Berkeley's OS course repo:
```
    # This line is needed because the ubuntu/bionic64 Vagrantfile sets the
    # file to one hardcoded based on the directory where "vagrant up" is
    # originally run, preventing distribution. Simply using "--uartmode1
    # disconnected" causes the VM to boot 100x to 1000x more slowly on some
    # versions of VirtualBox (e.g., 6.0.2), causing vagrant to time out. See
    # https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/issues/10578.
    # The fix for now is to require students to use a version of VirtualBox
    # without this problem. Version 6.0.10, the latest verion of VirtualBox at
    # the time of writing, appears not to have such problems.
    vb.customize ["modifyvm", :id, "--uartmode1", "disconnected"]
```

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 19:59 UTC

This sounds like the issue we are seeing here.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 20:09 UTC

And yeah from the VB docs this line is setting the `COM1: I/O base 0x3F8` serial port as disconnected.  Which is equivalent to disconnecting a virtual cable.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 20:12 UTC

Also, here is the issue [referenced](https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/issues/10578) in the above block.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 20:48 UTC

I'm checking to see if I get this with VirtualBox 6.0.x

Using VirtualBox 6.0.22 ([released May 15th](https://www.virtualbox.org/wiki/Changelog-6.0#v22)) and Vagrant 2.2.9, I have no issues building the guest.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 21:26 UTC

Seeing if I can repro with VB 6.1.8

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 21:28 UTC

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 21:29 UTC

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-19 21:32 UTC

I'm not caring about either, was just testing the hashicorp vs ubuntu to confirm the problem related to ubuntu.

**Hendrik Visage** · 2020-05-20 07:15 UTC

(replying to Wyatt Hoodes)
> Also you can see if a log file is generated in the project's root after building the VM using a different box, and if not I think we could remove the `uartmode1` line as well.

Seems the Ubuntu/bionic64 does write a logfile when that line is removed, and then barfs if the uart isn't there to write out that log file
(And when you do things headless, such a log file isn't necessarily unnecessary, as it's great to see whether things broke with that boot up, which isn't quite that simple when using vagrant that start headless)
being a sysadmin, I prefer that log file to be able to debug quicker  ;)

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-05-20 14:10 UTC

> Seems the Ubuntu/bionic64 does write a logfile when that line is removed, and then barfs if the uart isn't there to write out that log file

All of this behavior is explained via the commit message that Tim linked, code comments, and sources referenced in this thread.

> I prefer that log file to be able to debug quicker

I appreciate that, but one can just use `--debug` with Vagrant if they want a log to look at.

So, I think it's pretty clear from this thread that we want to switch to the hashicorp base box.

## tools/renumber-migrations

*2020-06-18 to 2020-06-18 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/tools.2Frenumber-migrations/with/908600)*

**Clara Dantas** · 2020-06-18 18:27 UTC

I mistyped  and messed up some migrations orders while executing `./tools/renumber-migrations` is there a way that I can undo that, other than editing by hand?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-18 18:39 UTC

@Clara Dantas well, you can always just copy the new migration you've added, `git checkout upstream/master zerver/migrations` to reset those directories to master, and then redo the process.  

If you had a Git commit with your old migration, you can restore your state using `git reflog`, which is why I'd usually do :)

**Clara Dantas** · 2020-06-18 18:41 UTC

aaah cool! Thanks! :slight_smile:

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-07-20 21:39 UTC

@ReCore Don’t use `sudo` with `vagrant`. Using `sudo` has probably changed the permissions in part of your zulip checkout such that your normal user is unable to access it. You might try to fix it with `sudo vagrant destroy; sudo chown -R $(id -un): .` in your zulip checkout, or delete it and clone it again. If there’s still a permission error, still don’t use `sudo`; you’ll need to figure out what actually happened and fix it in some other way.

## node_modules in vagrant and host os

*2020-07-28 to 2020-07-28 · 26 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/node_modules.20in.20vagrant.20and.20host.20os/with/959893)*

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 15:36 UTC

Can we somehow share `node_modules` between vagrant and the host os? Because currently `node_modules` is a broken symlink in the host os. This would be very useful for debugging puppeteer test with chromium visible (since vagrant doesn't support gui).

CC @Anders Kaseorg

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-28 17:44 UTC

Good question.  I could imagine adding /srv/zulip as a shared folder

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-28 17:44 UTC

But that will likely not work because you'll need the venv too.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-28 17:45 UTC

And that's very unlikely to work shared with the host OS given different pythons, libc, etc.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-28 17:46 UTC

I wonder if one can configure puppeteer to x forward the chromium or something?

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 17:46 UTC

I just want to run the puppeteer tests in my host os and the backend in vagrant. The puppeteer tests just need `node_modules` (no Python or venv).

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 17:50 UTC

hmm, I think moving the `node_modules` folder in vagrant elsewhere would suffice. This way you could just run the backend as usual with vagrant and do `npm install` in the host os. (This would also probably be better for Windows users since afaik Linux `node_modules` probably don't work on Windows.)

**Priyank Patel** · 2020-07-28 18:34 UTC

You can't really move `node_modules` location without leaving a symlink in place otherwise `require` in node tests and elsewhere will fail. What does not work when you run `npm install` or `yarn install` in host os outside vagrant? (I expect provision to remove the node_module you added from outside.)

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 18:37 UTC

I didn't add a node_modules. The node_modules symlink from Vagrant is in the directory of the host OS as a broken symlink `node_modules -> /srv/zulip-npm-cache/3a803f9969fc8fc6aff36001a7014ba54e7b7c67/node_modules`, which makes npm commands fail.

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 18:39 UTC

>You can't really move node_modules location

I think you totally can with the `NODE_PATH` environment variable.

**Priyank Patel** · 2020-07-28 18:44 UTC

I guess it would not be an ideal solution for webpack stuff if it has problem with the node_modules not being present though.

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 18:47 UTC

I am not familiar with the intricacies of webpack, but a quick search yields that we could [configure a resolveLoader](https://webpack.js.org/configuration/resolve/#resolveloader).

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-28 18:53 UTC

I expect you could run `provision` outside the development environment and share the checkout, but that has its own downsides.

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 18:54 UTC

I think never creating a broken `node_modules` symlink in the host os when using vagrant would result in the best developer experience.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-28 18:54 UTC

Another direction would be to try adding another `config.vm.synced_folder` setting.

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 18:55 UTC

That wouldn't work for Windows users since node_modules are platform dependent.

**Priyank Patel** · 2020-07-28 19:02 UTC

I think the platform dependencies are only a problem for native modules. That can be solved by running `npm rebuild` and `yarn rebuild` afterward inside vagrant. But, in this case, you only need puppeteer so that won't be an issue.

I should also mention that the `.bin` the folder is also an issue but again someone would need that in this case so this is fine too. Of course, there could be other problems too.

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 19:03 UTC

Afaik puppeteer needs a native binary for chromium (if you don't configure it to use your system-wide chromium).

**Priyank Patel** · 2020-07-28 19:04 UTC

Well, it installs that (as opposed to building it which `npm rebuild` can fix) so one could just run the install thing we do in `tools/test-js-with-puppeteer` and get that.

**Priyank Patel** · 2020-07-28 19:07 UTC

You will want to remove, `node_modules/.bin/chromium` and puppeteer will automatically install windows chromium for you when you run it.

**Priyank Patel** · 2020-07-28 19:09 UTC

So we manually call `puppeteer/install.js` if `node_modules/.bin/chromium` is not present.

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 19:10 UTC

I want to run all puppeteer tests in headless mode in vagrant and specific puppeteer tests in the host os in non-headless mode. I want to be able to do both in succession without having to manipulate my node_modules.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-28 19:11 UTC

I agree that's a good expression of a goal we should have here.

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-28 19:18 UTC

hmm, if the puppeteer binary is really the only problem we could maybe make `node_modules` a synced folder and in vagrant download chromium elsewhere and use the `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` environment variable

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-07-28 19:43 UTC

I still think our `node_modules` symlink and cache system solves a nonexistent problem while creating a number of existent ones. `yarn` has its own caches and it’s quite fast, at least if you aren’t sabotaging it by running it on a fresh directory every time.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-28 19:47 UTC

It's perhaps worth doing some timing testing to evaluate the performance side of that hypothesis.  I suppose we could keep the "Track the hash of the current build" logic to keep `provision` fast were we to change this.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-12-21 11:14 UTC

In any sufficiently UNIX-like system, including Git Bash, `~` expands to your home directory. Run `echo ~` to see where that is. Do not add `.txt`.

**Nikhil Maske (nikhilmaske-2001)** · 2020-12-21 11:39 UTC

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2020-12-21 12:10 UTC

@Nikhil Maske  Create a file named ```.zulip-vagrant-config``` containing that line. Don't add any extensions to it. Place it in your home directory. So, if your username is ```nikhil```, place the file at /home/nikhil.
Or you can just run this command from anywhere:
```
echo "VBOXADD_VERSION 6.0.4" > ~/.zulip-vagrant-config
```

```bash

vagrant ssh

./tools/provision
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-11-09 22:36 UTC

The purpose is the `O_EXCL`, which was not supported by Python’s builtin `open` until Python 3.3. I’ve had a local commit simplifying that sitting in a larger WIP branch for a while: #16729.

The issue was weird in the first place. :sweat_smile:

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-11-10 03:39 UTC

The syscall difference is that `open(…, "x")` does an `openat(AT_FDCWD, …, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_CLOEXEC, 0666)` syscall instead of `openat(AT_FDCWD, …, O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_CLOEXEC, 0444)`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-11-10 03:39 UTC

So maybe there’s a VirtualBox bug with `O_RDWR | O_EXCL`.

EC2 instances are behind a firewall (AWS security group) by default. You need to open port 9991.
