## Vagrant ssh fail (selinux?)

*2021-01-26 to 2021-01-26 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Vagrant.20ssh.20fail.20.28selinux.3F.29/with/1107172)*

**Robert (ro-i)** · 2021-01-26 18:34 UTC

Hi :smile: Does anyone happen to know something about the following error?
```
(ins)[~/dev/github/zulip]$ vagrant provision 
==> default: Running provisioner: shell...
    default: Running: inline script
    default: ++ set -e
    default: ++ set -o pipefail
    default: ++ '[' '!' '' ']'
    default: ++ sudo ln -nsf /srv/zulip/tools/setup/dev-motd /etc/update-motd.d/99-zulip-dev
    default: ++ sudo rm -f /etc/update-motd.d/10-help-text
    default: ++ sudo dpkg --purge landscape-client landscape-common ubuntu-release-upgrader-core update-manager-core update-notifier-common ubuntu-server
    default: dpkg: warning: ignoring request to remove landscape-client which isn't installed
    default: dpkg: warning: ignoring request to remove landscape-common which isn't installed
    default: dpkg: warning: ignoring request to remove ubuntu-release-upgrader-core which isn't installed
    default: dpkg: warning: ignoring request to remove update-manager-core which isn't installed
    default: dpkg: warning: ignoring request to remove update-notifier-common which isn't installed
    default: dpkg: warning: ignoring request to remove ubuntu-server which isn't installed
    default: ++ sudo dpkg-divert --add --rename /etc/default/motd-news
    default: Leaving 'local diversion of /etc/default/motd-news to /etc/default/motd-news.distrib'
    default: ++ sudo sh -c 'echo ENABLED=0 > /etc/default/motd-news'
    default: ++ '[' -d /sys/fs/selinux ']'
    default: ++ sudo mount -o remount,ro /sys/fs/selinux
    default: mount: /sys/fs/selinux: permission denied.
The SSH command responded with a non-zero exit status. Vagrant
assumes that this means the command failed. The output for this command
should be in the log above. Please read the output to determine what
went wrong.
```

I am running Fedora 33, my user is part of the `docker` group, and the `selinux` status is:
```
(ins)[~]$ sestatus 
SELinux status:                 enabled
SELinuxfs mount:                /sys/fs/selinux
SELinux root directory:         /etc/selinux
Loaded policy name:             targeted
Current mode:                   enforcing
Mode from config file:          enforcing
Policy MLS status:              enabled
Policy deny_unknown status:     allowed
Memory protection checking:     actual (secure)
Max kernel policy version:      33
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-26 18:45 UTC

@Robert the error is that your selinux policy is preventing Vagrant from mounting /sys/fs/selinux read-only inside the guest, which I imagine is required for the guest to work properly (though I didn't write that specific code).

```

    default: ++ sudo mount -o remount,ro /sys/fs/selinux
    default: mount: /sys/fs/selinux: permission denied.
```

**Robert (ro-i)** · 2021-01-26 19:23 UTC

@Tim Abbott Ok, thank you! Is there any workaround for this beyond changing the selinux policy globally?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-01-26 19:28 UTC

We can likely just delete that block. It’s five years old and predates multiple Ubuntu upgrades and our switch from LXC to Docker.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-01-26 19:31 UTC

Try deleting these lines from `Vagrantfile`, and if it works for you I’m happy to push this change.

```diff
--- a/Vagrantfile
+++ b/Vagrantfile
@@ -158,12 +158,6 @@ sudo dpkg --purge landscape-client landscape-common ubuntu-release-upgrader-core
 sudo dpkg-divert --add --rename /etc/default/motd-news
 sudo sh -c 'echo ENABLED=0 > /etc/default/motd-news'
 
-# If the host is running SELinux remount the /sys/fs/selinux directory as read only,
-# needed for apt-get to work.
-if [ -d "/sys/fs/selinux" ]; then
-    sudo mount -o remount,ro /sys/fs/selinux
-fi
-
 # Set default locale, this prevents errors if the user has another locale set.
 if ! grep -q 'LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8' /etc/default/locale; then
     echo "LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8" | sudo tee -a /etc/default/locale
```

**Robert (ro-i)** · 2021-01-26 20:46 UTC

@Anders Kaseorg Worked!
`    default: Zulip development environment setup succeeded!`
Thank you! :thumbs_up:

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-01-26 20:58 UTC

Excellent. Opened #17129.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-26 21:14 UTC

And merged, so you can get the fix by just `git pull --rebase` @Robert rather than needing to maintain it locally.

*2021-02-11 to 2021-02-12 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Unable.20to.20locate.20package.20certbot/with/1116262)*

Does anyone else get the error `Unable to locate package certbot` when the ENV variable `SSL_CERTIFICATE_GENERATION: 'certbot'` in the docker-compose file?

**alxjsn** · 2021-02-11 01:05 UTC

Looks like that package isn't available when it does the apt-get install?

**alxjsn** · 2021-02-11 01:16 UTC

```zulip_1      | Generating LetsEncrypt/certbot certificate ...
zulip_1      | + case " $os_id $os_id_like " in
zulip_1      | + apt-get install -y certbot

zulip_1      | E: Unable to locate package certbot

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-12 01:10 UTC

@alxjsn did you fork the Docker file?  I would have expected it to be getting `certbot` directly from the upstream Ubuntu.

**alxjsn** · 2021-02-12 01:19 UTC

I used the image `zulip/docker-zulip:3.3-0` from docker hub

**alxjsn** · 2021-02-12 01:19 UTC

I ended up modifying the Dockerfile to include certbot during the apt-get install: `apt-get -q install --no-install-recommends -y certbot ca-certificates git locales lsb-release python3 sudo tzdata` and built my own image

**alxjsn** · 2021-02-12 01:20 UTC

That ended up fixing the issue for me

**alxjsn** · 2021-02-12 01:21 UTC

```python3
def clean_cache_script_args(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    # Keep this in sync with parse_cache_script_args in zulip_tools.py.
    DEFAULT_ARGS = {
    "threshold_days": 14,
    "dry_run": False,
    "no_headings": False,
    "verbose": False
    }

    for arg in DEFAULT_ARGS.keys():
        if not getattr(args, arg, None):
            setattr(args, arg, DEFAULT_ARGS[arg])

    args.verbose |= args.dry_run  # Always print a detailed report in case of dry run.
```

Failed to build google-re2
```

The issue here is that in order to build the  google-re2 package, pybind11 must be installed first. As noted in the re2 source: https://github.com/google/re2/blob/abseil/python/setup.py. I suspect this problem was not discovered because there are wheels for x86_64 (https://pypi.org/project/google-re2/0.2.20210901/#files), but not for other architectures: I am running Zulip dev on an aarch64 processor.

I'm not familiar enough yet with the setup to know the "correct" way to fix this, but I was able to resolve and confirm the fix by adding the pybind11 package locally.

**Benson Muite** · 2021-10-16 16:38 UTC

Tried this on Oracle cloud and got it to work. Their free tier will allow you to deploy a 1 core 6GB Ram instance with Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. The steps I followed are:
Steps

1) Launch an Ampere instance with 1 core and 6 GB or Ram.
2) Get the public IP address of the instance and point a domain name to it
3) Make sure ports 22, 80 and 443 are open in the Oracle Virtual cloud network
4) Log in to your Ampere instance by SSH
5) ssh -i PATH_TO_SSH_KEY ubuntu@ip.address
6) $ sudo apt-get update
7) $ sudo apt-get install -y python3-pybind11
8) $ cd $(mktemp -d)
9) $ curl -fLO https://download.zulip.com/server/zulip-server-latest.tar.gz
10) $ tar -xf zulip-server-latest.tar.gz
11) $ sudo -s
12) $ iptables -I INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
13) $ iptables -I INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
14) $ wget https://github.com/google/re2/archive/refs/tags/2021-09-01.tar.gz
15) $ tar -xvf 2021-09-01.tar.gz
16) $ cd re2-2021-09-01/
17) $  make
18) $  make test
19) $  make install
20) $  make testinstall
21) $ cd ..
22) $ ./zulip-server-4.7/scripts/setup/install --certbot --email=my@email.address --hostname=chat.domain.name

**Uzair Ali** · 2021-11-16 14:01 UTC

Hey There!!
I've just completed Zulip's Dev setup using vagrant and completed it but however zulip loads without CSS
[Screenshot-from-2021-11-16-19-28-21.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/c0/q8EbAA9eQk4W3bHD6CRZiEAR/Screenshot-from-2021-11-16-19-28-21.png) 

The only change i did was :
From
`host_port = 9991`
To
`host_port = 8080`
in vagrant file

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-16 20:53 UTC

@Uzair Ali I suspect the problem has to do with your port change; if I had to guess, `webpack` (which serves CSS, among other things) is not being reached by your browser properly.

Why the change in port?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-16 20:53 UTC

My guess is you need to change additional configuration in the development environment so that it knows its EXTERNAL_HOST is different to make a variant port work.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-11-16 21:05 UTC

I don't see how this could have ever worked. Changing host_port to 8080 causes Vagrant to forward the host's port 8083 to the Webpack running on the guest's port 9994, but there's nothing that attempts to tell the browser to make requests to Webpack on port 8083.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-16 21:15 UTC

This feature predated Webpack, and pre-webpack, we connected to everything through the `run-dev.py` proxy on port 9991.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-16 21:15 UTC

So I think this broke in like 2018 when we migrated to webpack, and nobody's tried to use it since then before today.

**Mounil Shah (mounilKshah)** · 2022-01-16 10:47 UTC

**BIKI DAS** · 2022-01-16 13:27 UTC

(replying to shahil ramchandani)
> I clone Zulip repository but i got these and not able to clone how i clone? [Screenshot-89.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/c8/JS4w-gaebbCiKLHoKx9XJqLz/Screenshot-89.png)
Hello @shahil ramchandani , you might have gone wrong somewhere ,try to follow the step below-

1.first go to github and make sure you have forked the repo and copied the clone code from the forked one.
2.then git clone followed by your forked clone code , it should work fine
3. then type git remote -v, you will get to see the remote repos, here you need to add the master/main repo so that  you remain in sync with the repo and avoid merge conflicts
4.type git remote add upstream followed by the  code of the main repo
5.following these steps you are all done and you can again do a git remote -v to check if your upstream has been set correctly or not

if you face any problems, ping me up.

**Adam Sah** · 2022-01-25 12:59 UTC

heads-up, Mac  OSX 12.1 Monterey docker Engine 20.10.12 (desktop 4.4.2), sync'd to main, ran `vagrant destroy` and `vagrant up` and got the dreaded `Error running a subcommand of ./tools/lib/provision.py` which I tracked down to this curl crashing (!): `curl -fLO https://registry.npmjs.org/yarn/-/yarn-1.22.17.tgz` ([install-yarn:21](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/scripts/lib/install-yarn#L21)). **Mohit Gupta** · 2022-02-05 20:39 UTC

(replying to Mohit Gupta)
> Got similar issue: After digging found out that it's Known docker issue: https://docs.docker.com/desktop/mac/release-notes/3.x/#known-issues It seems to be related to libssl that comes with OS image. In file `tools/setup/dev-vagrant-docker/Dockerfile`
changed `FROM debian:10` to `FROM debian:11`

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-02-05 22:32 UTC

See #20910. Until the Debian OpenSSL package gets updated, you can use [this workaround](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/20910#issuecomment-1021795877) on Debian 10.

That’s #20910. Use the following workaround for now:

```sh
vagrant ssh
sudo perl -0777 -pe 's/(\xbf#\x03\xd5)(\xfd\x07E\xf8)/$2$1/' \
    -i /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libcrypto.so.1.1
tools/provision
```

**Evy** · 2022-02-16 21:39 UTC

I was trying to think through that. I wish I remember what my original issue with `vagrant destroy` was, but here are some things I had to figure out that I didn't explicitly find in the docs:

* what to do for the 18.04 issue specifically - the answer being "vagrant destroy and create a new one"
* what to do when you see the error `Stderr: Error response from daemon: dial unix  [...]docker.raw.sock: connect: connection refused`-- the answer being "Docker is probably not running. **Tim Abbott** · 2022-02-16 21:41 UTC

I think you should have gotten an error message when trying to provision on an 18.04 system with that `vagrant destroy` output.  It's also a one-time transition that was announced prominently in chat.zulip.org, so mainly affects folks who'd been inactive for a while.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-02-16 21:42 UTC

Specifically this code:
```
os="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$ID $VERSION_ID")"
case "$os" in
    'ubuntu 14.04' | 'ubuntu 16.04' | 'ubuntu 18.04')
        echo "Error: $os is no longer a supported platform for Zulip." >&2
        if [ -e /home/vagrant ]; then
            # shellcheck disable=SC2016
            echo 'To upgrade, run `vagrant destroy`, and then recreate the Vagrant guest.' >&2
            echo 'See: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-vagrant.html' >&2
        fi
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
```

## Bind mounts selinux context

*2022-05-29 to 2022-07-28 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Bind.20mounts.20selinux.20context/with/1386075)*

**Robert (ro-i)** · 2022-05-29 08:04 UTC

Hi :)
I recently re-installed my Zulip development environment (I'm on Fedora 36), and realized that it seems to be necessary now to consider the selinux context for the bind mounts because otherwise vagrant tells that it cannot write to the cloned Zulip repository.
Actually, I changed in `Vagrantfile`:
```diff
-  config.vm.synced_folder ".", "/vagrant", disabled: true
-  config.vm.synced_folder ".", "/srv/zulip"
+  config.vm.synced_folder ".", "/vagrant:z", disabled: true
+  config.vm.synced_folder ".", "/srv/zulip:z"
```
See https://docs.docker.com/storage/bind-mounts/#configure-the-selinux-label for the docs. (I use `moby-engine` on Fedora instead of the official docker packages, but I don't think that's an issue here...)

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-05-31 22:56 UTC

## Higher memory requirement

*2022-09-03 to 2022-09-13 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Higher.20memory.20requirement/with/1430146)*

**David Rosa** · 2022-09-03 23:45 UTC

I've set up my Zulip development environment with Vagrant + Docker on macOS. A few days ago, I noticed that the com.docker.hyperkit process was taking up around 13GB of memory. This seemed strange so I removed all images and containers.  I ran the provisioning process from scratch, and then I lowered docker's memory resource setting to 4GB.

**David Rosa** · 2022-09-03 23:46 UTC

I was expecting everything would work fine, but then I kept getting the error "Django cannot connect to Tornado server". Then eventually, I realized that Tornado kept crashing at startup because there wasn't enough memory. So I increased docker's memory resource setting until Tornado finally worked at 7GB.

**David Rosa** · 2022-09-03 23:47 UTC

So now the com.docker.hyperkit process is taking about half as much memory than before, but it's still higher than I would've expected. I'm curious about how much memory the docker process is consuming in other systems. I'd be great if other people could share this info. I'm also curious about how much memory the vagrant + docker setup takes up on Linux and Windows.

**David Rosa** · 2022-09-03 23:48 UTC

We should probably update or add a note to the [Requirements](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-vagrant.html#requirements) and [Troubleshooting and common errors](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-vagrant.html#troubleshooting-and-common-errors) sections to document the scenario described above.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-09-07 22:52 UTC

@David Rosa we should investigate what's happening here. It would be fairly surprising for the development environment to require 7GB of RAM; we run Zulip servers in production on ~2GB, and while that does't run `webpack`, something needs to be very wrong for that to take 5GB of RAM.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-09-07 22:52 UTC

Are you seeing this on `main` or on a branch you're working on?

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-09-07 22:53 UTC

In any use, running `ps aux` inside your Zulip environment would be helpful for debugging what is consuming the RAM here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-09-07 22:53 UTC

It's very possible that we have a regression, but the right thing to do would be to fix it, not document it :).

**Matt** · 2022-09-08 12:39 UTC

My local dev (vagrant/docker on Linux, 64GB RAM) is unconstrained and sits at ~1.5G (1G is webpack) *after* an initial balloon of webpack to 6G. MacOS may be reporting the virtual memory  versus the resident memory. Virtually speaking the stack is using ~50G.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-09-08 20:23 UTC

Hmm, Webpack should not be ballooning to 6G, so if it is, that could be a regression.

*2022-10-06 to 2022-10-06 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20Facing.20trouble.20with.20docker.20on.20manjaro.20.28arch.20based.29/with/1445446)*

**Om Srivastava❄** · 2022-10-06 06:31 UTC

Hello everyone, a newbie here!
I am following the guide to installing vagrant setup in the guide given here: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-recommended.html
Now, when I get to the step `vagrant up --provider=docker`, I get an error with docker saying

Command: ["docker", "build", "--build-arg", "VAGRANT_UID=1000", "/home/umang/padhi likhi/Development/zulip/zulip/tools/setup/dev-vagrant-docker", {:notify=>[:stdout, :stderr]}]

Stderr: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)

I searched around the web and saw that to test if docker is correctly installed, I should try running `docker pull hello-world && docker run hello-world`, I still get the error - Error response from daemon: Head "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/hello-world/manifests/latest": Get "https://auth.docker.io/token?scope=repository%3Alibrary%2Fhello-world%3Apull&service=registry.docker.io": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)

Can anyone tell me how to solve this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-10-06 19:33 UTC

@Om Srivastava that error sounds like Docker is having trouble accessing the Internet; usually that is indeed a situation where your computer is on a network where a proxy is required to access the general Internet. I would try again using a different network if you have another option available.

## postgres 10 desupported

*2022-10-07 to 2022-10-07 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/postgres.2010.20desupported/with/1445947)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-10-07 00:42 UTC

Just an FYI, for those of us whose development environments are very old, one might get this error provisioning when you next rebase:
```
django.db.utils.NotSupportedError: PostgreSQL 11 or later is required (found 10.19).
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-10-07 00:44 UTC

I don't think we have documentation on upgrading postgres in the development environment. For folks using Vagrant, rebuilding the image should work fine if necessary, which I expect to be rare; you're only going to run into this if you did an `do-release-upgrade` or equivalent on a system originally installed with postgres 10.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-10-07 00:44 UTC

Such a development environment is probably running Ubuntu 18.04 and thus was already desupported last year.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-10-07 00:45 UTC

Indeed, I seem to have both postgres 10 and 12 installed.
```
$ dpkg -l | grep 'postgresql-1[0-9] '
ii  postgresql-10                              10.19-2.pgdg20.04+1                   amd64        The World's Most Advanced Open Source Relational Database
ii  postgresql-12                              12.9-2.pgdg20.04+1                    amd64        The World's Most Advanced Open Source Relational Database
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-10-07 00:47 UTC

Uninstalling and purging both, `rm -rf zulip/var/` to clear `provision`'s cache of which steps its run,  then running `provision` should do the right thing.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-10-07 00:54 UTC

OK, that indeed worked.

* Read the error log and then got an idea what was causing an error
* Opened ```zulip\tools\setup/postgresql-init-dev-db```

**Josh Klar** · 2023-01-07 09:45 UTC

On a Unix/Linux/Mac/WSL system you should effectively *always* run *all* commands as a non-root user without sudo/doas, unless you are very sure you actually must escalate privileges to accomplish whatever you're trying to do (for example, updating system-wide configurations or packages). **Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-01-11 18:28 UTC

>  I made a new user in ubuntu, I had some doubts.

I don't think there's a need to create a new user in ubuntu for setting up the development environment.

When `Josh Klar` said:

> On a Unix/Linux/Mac/WSL system you should effectively always run all commands as a non-root user without sudo/doas

It means, running all your commands **without prefixing** it with `sudo` (unless you're sure, why you're using sudo) while following the installation docs of zulip.

Extras to make things a bit clear:
* The sudo package is pre-installed on most Linux distributions.
* The sudo command allows you to run programs as another user, by default the root user.
* Using sudo instead of login in as root is more secure because you can grant limited administrative privileges to individual users without them knowing the root password.
* The root user account in Ubuntu is disabled by default for security reasons, and users are encouraged to perform system administrative tasks using sudo.
* The initial user created by the Ubuntu installer is already granted sudo privileges.

**Hence,**
If you want to run any command as a non-root user simply run the `command`
but, if you want to run a command as the root user, prefix the command with sudo i.e `sudo command`

Anyway, try to [find what is currently binding that port and kill it](https://stackoverflow.com/a/39974485) - whether it's a Zulip dev server or some other service you have running on your machine, something is bound to the port in question, as the error message in your screenshot shows. ## Yarn integrity check failing

*2023-01-30 to 2023-01-30 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Yarn.20integrity.20check.20failing/with/1499356)*

**Steve Gattuso** · 2023-01-30 20:22 UTC

Hi everyone,

While trying to get Zulip setup locally I ran into an issue that I don't *think* is related to the project, but I wanted to get down either way just to have some kind of documentation for if/when someone sees it in the future. It looks like this particular issue popped up in a test failure [here](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/43-automated-testing/topic/main.20failing/near/1499313), so I suspect I'm not the only person dealing with this.

Specifically, when running `vagrant provision` I was seeing the following failure crop up in the `yarn install` step:

```
   default: + SKIP_VENV_SHELL_WARNING=1
    default: + set +x
    default: No changes to apt dependencies, so skipping apt operations.
    default: + sudo -H -- env http_proxy= https_proxy= no_proxy= scripts/lib/install-node
    default: + sudo -- env http_proxy= https_proxy= no_proxy= scripts/lib/install-yarn
    default: Cached version not found! Installing node modules.
    default: + /srv/zulip-yarn/bin/yarn install --non-interactive --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline
    default: yarn install v1.22.19
    default: [1/4] Resolving packages...
    default: [2/4] Fetching packages...
    default: error https://codeload.github.com/andersk/postcss-media-minmax/tar.gz/92c4dd33b9add115ec436ef25243484cca0f7355: Integrity check failed for "postcss-media-minmax" (computed integrity doesn't match our records, got "sha512-PWzNmdhQCE21oT7J5vj3fUbbywphh9zXP3aoxRsu8M5pjAPxQW8JVBdTFWHXQ8LTTomKmnt9lW2SZBBymQFu3g== sha1-iX+MOkPfwugi3LnzmOsZeIgPO/U=")
    default: info Visit https://yarnpkg.com/en/docs/cli/install for documentation about this command.
    default:
    default: Error running a subcommand of ./lib/provision.py: /srv/zulip-yarn/bin/yarn install --non-interactive --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline
    default: Actual error output for the subcommand is just above this.
    default:
    default:
    default: Provisioning failed (exit code 1)!
    default:
    default: * Look at the traceback(s) above to find more about the errors.
    default: * Resolve the errors or get help on chat.
    default: * If you can fix this yourself, you can re-run tools/provision at any time.
    default: * Logs are here: zulip/var/log/provision.log
    default:
The SSH command responded with a non-zero exit status. Vagrant
assumes that this means the command failed. The output for this command
should be in the log above. Please read the output to determine what
went wrong.
```

I've only copied in a slice of the full provisioning log for brevity, but I'm happy to provide more context if needed.

Funny enough, I've been able to resolve the issue since I started writing this out (hooray rubber duck debugging) by running `yarn install` on my *host machine* and then re-running `vagrant provision`. I'm not sure exactly why this fixes the issue (maybe yarn's servers fixed itself in between the VM run and my host machine run?), but either way it's been smooth sailing since then.

Anyways, no action needed here but I figured this would be good to document since I didn't see any search results about it as I was trying to debug.

**Josh Klar** · 2023-03-02 09:10 UTC

marking this unread to check out in the morning; I don't use an M1/ARM64 machine as my daily driver but I do have access to a few for testing; I'll see if I can repro

our dependencies are version-locked so I suspect that *either* (1) we recently upgraded dependencies, and the commit that did the upgrade could be rolled back, or (2) this has been a recurring/longer-running arm64-specific bug that may impact more than "the latest release"

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-03-02 15:57 UTC

We last upgraded dependencies on February 3rd -- and the version of `line-profiler` hasn't changed since March 24th 2022, so it's not a version change in `line-profiler`.

https://github.com/pyutils/line_profiler/issues/204 points to it being a problem with cython.  Which I don't have installed on my Linux box, nor is it pinned in our dependencies, presumably because it's a build-time dependency because there aren't prebuilt wheels for `line-profiler` for the M1?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-03-02 16:05 UTC

I can reproduce the error if I build from the `line-profiler` repo.  https://github.com/pyutils/line_profiler/pull/203/commits/15a12f98faf067bc149d5c478305b44a31bc4a54 is nominally the fix but is part of a larger series, so doesn't cherry-pick onto main cleanly.  I'll see if I can massage it into a minimal fix.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-03-02 16:27 UTC

Pushed https://github.com/pyutils/line_profiler/pull/205 which they'll need to merge.

This time I did generated and add the ssh key to my github account. This was the only difference perhaps. Now I am able to run a development environment [Cheers!]
PS: I didn't need vagrant as I was using WSL2 on windows 11

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-07 02:11 UTC

@Hardik Dharmani so I think the core of the import cycle here is that `overlays.js` probably doesn't need to import `popovers.js` -- it just calls `popovers.hide_all`, and we can probably make that work via triggering a "hide popovers" event rather than a direct call if need be.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-07 02:12 UTC

The `overlays` module does not otherwise have a lot of dependencies.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-07 02:12 UTC

I suppose there's a couple ways we could make `popovers.hide_all` get called when opening/closing an overlay.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-07 02:15 UTC

I think one may that might feel nice is to have an `overlays.register_pre_open_hook` and `overlays.register_pre_close_hook`, and have a new `popovers.initialize` method (called from `ui_init.js`) call `overlays.register_pre_open_hook(popovers.hide_all);`. (And then have a loop call all such registered hooks at the start of `open_overlay` and `close_overlay`).

`popovers.js` imports `overlays.js` directly already, so that'll also remove an extremely direct import loop where each of those modules import the other.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-07 02:17 UTC

Yeah, doing this as also the only blocker to converting `overlays.js` to TypeScript (well, we need to convert `browser_history.js` to TypeScript first). It might make sense for you to a separate prep PR to clean up this dependency cycle -- it'll be nice to do review and integration of that independent of the particular feature you're working on that happens to want us to break the cycle.

**Hardik Dharmani** · 2023-03-09 08:28 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-09 16:29 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-09 16:30 UTC

Haven't looked at the import there.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-10 00:35 UTC

@Hardik Dharmani OK, having looked, I think that import cycle issue is indeed that `unread.js` shouldn't be calling into `recent_topics_ui.js`. It does so just in one place in `update_message_for_mention`, to trigger a rerender. I think the fix is likely to do a refactor to make `update_message_for_mention` return `true/false` depending on whether the mention state for the target message changed (and thus a rerender of the message may be warranted), and have the callers be responsible for actually doing the rerendering.

**Hardik Dharmani** · 2023-03-10 19:26 UTC

(replying to Hardik Dharmani)
> Additionally, I have a question regarding the dependency cycles. Specifically, why does only the upload_widget calling the dialog_widget result in a dependency cycle error, while the other dependency cycles (such as``` ./overlays:8 => ./browser_history:5 => ./hash_util:2 => ./stream_data:5 => ./stre …
I believe I have found the answer to this question. The reason is that `uploadwidget.ts` is a TypeScript file and, as a rule, TypeScript does not allow dependency cycles. This is why other dependency cycles were not causing errors, as they were in JavaScript modules. Am I correct?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-10 19:31 UTC

Yes. (It was our decision, not TypeScript’s, to apply this rule only to TypeScript files in #24475. We could decide to alter this, but I don’t think we want to.)

After resolving one dependency cycle, I discovered another one. Even if I solve this particular cycle, there may still be several others that are not currently causing errors since they are in JavaScript modules (I have personally found two or three more). However, I believe these cycles will be resolved as we migrate our JavaScript codebase to TypeScript as part of the GSoC project "Migrate our JavaScript codebase to TypeScript."

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-10 19:40 UTC

Right, we have hundreds of cycles at present (#**frontend>cyclical dependencies**) and we want to get rid of them. Prohibiting them in TypeScript is a way to force ourselves to encounter them and remove them incrementally.

**Aniyar Durmagambetova** · 2023-03-11 17:24 UTC

Just fixed the issue, if anyone encounters the same thing, you should:
1) check `which python`
2) if it is anaconda, go to `home/path/to/anaconda/lib/pythonX.X/site-packages`
3) `rm -r scripts`

basically,  the scripts directory that we just removed was shown to python instead of the `zulip/scripts` directory.  It also only contains an empty init file so i think it's ok to delete

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-03-20 14:24 UTC

I can't replicate, even after blowing away node and the npm cache.  Does a force-reprovision fix it for you?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-20 16:48 UTC

Webpack stores a cache in `node_modules/.cache/webpack`. Changing the Node.js version has changed the hash that `tools/provision` uses to compute which `node_modules` symlink to use, so as a side effect, you got a different cache directory, even though the new Node.js doesn’t really have anything to do with it. You can just delete `node_modules/.cache/webpack` instead.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-20 16:55 UTC

I’ve seen traces like that occasionally, but I haven’t tried to investigate the underlying webpack bug. Maybe some kind of race condition that involves stopping webpack while it’s in the middle of rewriting the cache. It always fixes itself for me.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-03-20 18:27 UTC

Works fine after clearing `zulip-npm-cache`. Thanks!

1. check if pnpm is installed, using "pnpm --version".
2. If not installed run "npm install -g pnpm"
3. Then run "pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline"
4. run "vagrant up --provision"
This should solve the issue

**Raneh** · 2023-10-04 19:43 UTC

Hi everyone, I've been able to setup my zulip environment now. If you had the same error as I did(which looks like this: Subcommand of ./lib/provision.py failed with exit status 100: sudo -- env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install --allow-downgrades ) after entering ./tools/provision command. This was how I fixed the error:
1. After the provisioning failed. I ran this command : sudo dpkg --configure -a  to fix the interrupted installation.
2. Afterwards I ran this command again:  ./tools/provision

On Ubuntu: sudo apt install rabbitmq-server memcached redis-server postgresql

Ensure to start the following:
Check if rabbitmq is up and running. Enable management console:  sudo rabbitmq-plugins enable rabbitmq_management

Rabbitmq server:  sudo service rabbitmq-server restart

redis server:  sudo service redis-server start
postgresql database: sudo service postgresql start

then : ./tools/provision

**Beck00** · 2023-10-10 09:04 UTC

I hope I am not late. Here is a solution if you encounter this issue using WSL2 on windows

On Ubuntu: sudo apt install rabbitmq-server memcached redis-server postgresql

Ensure to start the following:
Check if rabbitmq is up and running. Enable management console: sudo rabbitmq-plugins enable rabbitmq_management

Rabbitmq server: sudo service rabbitmq-server restart

redis server: sudo service redis-server start
postgresql database: sudo service postgresql start

then : ./tools/provision

This is a known bug in macOS or Docker for Mac or pnpm, and it’s beyond my ability to debug further than what I’ve already reported to [Docker](https://github.com/docker/for-mac/issues/6787) and [pnpm](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5803#issuecomment-1490988892), with both macOS and Docker for Mac being proprietary. Stop using a proprietary operating system. But you can try switching the file system implementation to **osxfs (Legacy)** in Docker for Mac settings.

**Aditya Chaudhary** · 2025-02-23 05:16 UTC

this was a Corepack enabling issue. I was able to resolve it by running the following command:
`corepack prepare pnpm@8.7.0 --activate`

This ensures that the correct version of `pnpm` is activated and resolves the installation issue.
I hope this helps anyone facing the same problem! Let me know if you have any questions.

For more about the provision read this: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/dependencies.html#provisioning

After installing [WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/setup/environment), navigate to the Zulip codebase and run `./tools/provision` to set up dependencies. Start the server with `./tools/run-dev`, then open `http://localhost:9991` in your browser. If you face issues, check WSL network settings. For detailed steps, refer to the [Zulip Dev Setup Guide](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-recommended.html).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-12-10 20:47 UTC

Your output shows that `/media/bharat/New Volume` is of type `fuseblk`. That could mean any number of filesystem types, but the most popular one it could mean is NTFS-3G. If that’s what you’re using, you should be aware of that, should recognize that it’s an unusual configuration, and should have included that information in your report rather than making us guess.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-12-10 20:50 UTC

My understanding is that NTFS-3G supports POSIX permissions, but not by default. Its [documentation](https://github.com/tuxera/ntfs-3g/wiki/File-Ownership-and-Permissions) might help you figure out how to configure it correctly. But AFAIK nobody in the Zulip core team uses NTFS-3G, so we won’t be able to help you with it.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-12-10 20:51 UTC

I recommend setting up Zulip on a normal Linux filesystem within your home directory.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-29 20:36 UTC

Looking at that error message, I think it just sees that you previously tried to use `vagrant` and assumes it's a mistake:
```
if [ -e "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.vagrant" ] && [ ! -e /home/vagrant ]; then                  
    echo 'Error: provision should be run inside the Vagrant environment.' >&2                           
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016                                                                         
    echo 'Try `vagrant up --provision`.' >&2                                                            
    exit 1                                                                                              
fi                                                                                                      
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-29 20:37 UTC

So you can probably move aside your `~/.vagrant` folder to get past that error.

**Aditya Bajaj** · 2024-03-19 10:03 UTC

While I know this isn't a perfect fix to saving space, you could reduce the amount of space taken up by the code, specifically the `.git` directory by using `git clone --config pull.rebase git@github.com:<YOUR USERNAME>/zulip.git --depth=<DEPTH>`. 

<DEPTH> can be treated as the number of commits before `origin/HEAD` that you want to copy over to your local repo. This makes sense since you might not always need the entire commit history of the project.

Example storage savings: with `--depth=30`, the `.git` directory's size is ~100MB compared to ~450MB without specifying depth.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-03-19 13:42 UTC

We do not recommend doing this.  Specifically, cloning with `--depth` means that you do not get the full history of the project.  Being able to `git log` and find out *why* something is the way that it is is very important to working on a project of this size -- and one of the reasons that we are as picky as we are about commit messages and commit discipline is that it keeps that information high-signal.  Doing a shallow clone robs you of all of that valuable information.

**Aditya Bajaj** · 2024-03-19 14:22 UTC

I may have undervalued historical context for changes (and overvalued saving space😅) in my response. Thanks for the insight!

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-03-19 13:44 UTC

Something is interposing in your network between the Vagrant host and the contents it's trying to download, or the mirrors are in a corrupt state.  Fundamentally, the check that's failing is "did the file I download match the signed version that the mirror claimed it would give me."  Any failure in that is either a failure of the mirror's infrastructure, or a failure of the network between you and them.

**Aditya Bajaj** · 2024-03-20 09:14 UTC

The issue was likely caused by something hard to find so I'm explaining my solution below for anyone that runs into this in the future:

- I had screen time filtering settings for social media website on (found the webfilterproxyd process in Activity Monitor)
- Disabled all screen time settings completely. Killed the webfilterproxyd process in Activity Monitor
- Killed some unrelated vpn processes in Activity Monitor that I did not setup myself (they were run by root/system preferences, I'm unaware why)
- Restarted my system (I'd tried this before so it isn't simply restarting that fixed the issue for me)

Hope this helps someone in the future!

**Aditya Bajaj** · 2024-03-20 09:16 UTC

Thank you for trying to help with this @Alex Vandiver , it was your message that eventually led me to think of filtering through screen time :smile:

**Notification Bot** · 2024-03-20 09:17 UTC

@Aditya Bajaj has marked this topic as resolved.

I had to delete the codespace and create an entirely new one to get provision to run properly

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-04-05 21:30 UTC

I don’t expect you’ll have a good time trying to get this to work on GitHub Codespaces. If you do have further questions, though, please make sure to explain what you’re trying to do at the start of the conversation, not the end. **Tim Abbott** · 2024-05-13 23:37 UTC

I think you should be able to do load tests just fine with the development environment running inside Vagrant.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-05-13 23:40 UTC

But https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-advanced.html#installing-directly-on-ubuntu-debian-centos-or-fedora on an empty server might be more convenient.

There's differences in how the production environment is deployed, so it kinda depends on what you're trying to measure -- a speedup on individual endpoints or on the overall CPU load.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-05-13 23:40 UTC

https://github.com/zulip/docker-zulip is probably the easiest way to get a full production system on localhost with minimal hassle for load testing.

(replying to Shubham Ingale)
> @om pharate Is issue solved? I am also facing the issue.

I encountered the same error yesterday. I noticed that the rabbitmq-server and  postgresql  services weren't starting automatically, so I had to start them manually using the following commands:

1. Make sure the ports required by these services are not in use by other processes.

2. Start rabbitmq-server:
   
   sudo service rabbitmq-server start
  
   Check its status:
  
   sudo service rabbitmq-server status
   

3. Start  postgresql:
   bash
   sudo service postgresql start
   
   Check its status:
   
   sudo service postgresql status
   

4. After starting these services, run the provisioning command in the Zulip directory:
   ./tools/provision
   

5. Activate the virtual environment:

   source /srv/zulip-py3-venv/bin/activate


6. Finally, start the development server:

   ./tools/run-dev


This should help resolve the Bad-gateway issues.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2024-12-09 11:50 UTC

(replying to Harsh Kajalkhane)
> I encountered the same error yesterday. I noticed that the rabbitmq-server and postgresql services weren't starting automatically, so I had to start them manually using the following commands:

You can enable them to start them up automatically at boot time, using: 
```systemctl enable postgresql```
and 
```systemctl enable rabbitmq-server```

After enabling the services, you can verify they are active using `systemctl status postgresql` and `systemctl status rabbitmq-server`, etc.

Also, if you are running multiple wsl instances or running other dependencies locally on windows, port conflicts might prevent services from starting on your zulip wsl instance.
So make sure to terminate other instances using ```wsl -t``` prior to booting up your zulip wsl instance.

If some port conflicts even after shutting down other wsl instances, check the running services on windows for those ports using Powershell
```Get-Process -Id (Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <your_port_number>).OwningProcess```

If you find some process running on that port, you can kill it using 
``` taskkill /PID <pid> /F```

Here's an example with mysql running on port 3306 (assume its preventing mysql on wsl from starting)
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/fa/JbLfkXY_Hz8Vq6W_0MX6PRvJ/image.png)

@Tim Abbott , do you think this is worth mentioning in the wsl setup docs?
I had to figure this out myself. While it isn't very difficult to figure out, it might hinder the setup experience for new contributors.

```bash

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-08-02 17:38 UTC

It aborts if there's `.vagrant` in your Zulip checkout, and it's not running *inside* that Vagrant.

You can still provision directly if there's no `.vagrant` inside the Zulip checkout.

## ./tools/lint --fix takes forever

*2024-11-28 to 2024-11-28 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/.2E.2Ftools.2Flint.20--fix.20takes.20forever/with/1989900)*

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2024-11-28 08:28 UTC

I was working on composebox_typeahead.ts and the associated test file
Running prettier --write fixed the linting errors within a couple seconds, but ./tools/lint --fix was stuck for more than 5 mins after which i terminated the process.

I tried around half a dozen times, before using prettier

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-28 08:37 UTC

You can tell it which linter to fix with `--only=prettier`. Otherwise it has to rerun all of them, and do it without parallelism to prevent multiple fixes from corrupting each other.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-28 08:37 UTC

You can also tell it which files to fix. See `--help` for various useful options.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2024-11-28 08:40 UTC

Thanks for the information Anders,
I felt significant lag compared to other runs where I used this on the same files for the normal ./tools/lint without any `only` options

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-28 08:41 UTC

Without `--fix` it runs multiple linters in parallel.

@NISHAT ALAM ANSARI [napisał](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/SSH.20Authentication.20failure/near/1995748):
> **Subject: Issue with Zulip Development Setup on macOS M1 Using VirtualBox**

A great report by you. But you should first check what is going on Vagrant forum. They have issues to support both Docker and VirtualBox on machines with M1 cpu/soc.

Nothing to do with Zulip. And updating Ruby gems in your system is one of the ways to solve it (Vagrant is written in Ruby and they are a bit late with Go version which is going to solve similar issues).

    const pElements = document.querySelectorAll('p');

        const childNodes = [...pElement.childNodes];

        for (let i = 0; i < childNodes.length - 1; i+=1) {
            const currentNode = childNodes[i];
            const nextNode = childNodes[i + 1];

            if (!currentNode || !nextNode) {
                continue;
            }

            if (

}

should be in the log above. Please read the output to determine what
went wrong.
```
````

There was a helpful note in our setup doc, which I followed:

> **Important note**: There is a [known upstream issue on macOS](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/provision.20error.20ERR_PNPM_LINKING_FAILED/near/1649241) that can cause provisioning to fail with `ERR_PNPM_LINKING_FAILED` or other errors. The temporary fix is to open the Docker desktop app’s settings panel, and choose `osxfs (legacy)` under “Choose file sharing implementation for your containers.” Once Docker restarts, you should be able to successfully run `vagrant up --provider=docker`.

After changing that setting in Docker Desktop, I ran that command as requested. It was very fast; here's its output:

```
$ vagrant up --provider=docker
Bringing machine 'default' up with 'docker' provider...
==> default: Creating and configuring docker networks...
==> default: Image is already built from the Dockerfile. `vagrant reload` to rebuild.
==> default: Enabling network interfaces...
==> default: Starting container...
==> default: Waiting for machine to boot. This may take a few minutes...
    default: SSH address: 127.0.0.1:2222
    default: SSH username: vagrant
    default: SSH auth method: private key
    default: Warning: Remote connection disconnect. Retrying...
==> default: Machine booted and ready!
==> default: Machine already provisioned. Run `vagrant provision` or use the `--provision`
==> default: flag to force provisioning. Provisioners marked to run always will still run.
```

Note in particular "Machine already provisioned".

I ran `vagrant ssh`. Our setup doc helped me realize that the provisioning didn't actually succeed though:

> Congrats, you’re now inside the Zulip development environment! You can confirm this by looking at the command prompt, which starts with `(zulip-py3-venv)vagrant@`. If it just starts with `vagrant@`, your provisioning failed and you should look at the [troubleshooting section](https://zulip.readthedo …

See that the command prompt indeed just starts with `vagrant@`:

```
$ vagrant ssh
Welcome to Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (GNU/Linux 6.10.14-linuxkit aarch64)

This is the Zulip development environment.  Popular commands:
* tools/provision - Update the development environment
* tools/run-dev - Run the development server
* tools/lint - Run the linter (quick and catches many problems)
* tools/test-* - Run tests (use --help to learn about options)

Read https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/testing/testing.html to learn
how to run individual test suites so that you can get a fast debug cycle.

vagrant@8549f73d2fc2:~$ quit
-bash: quit: command not found
vagrant@8549f73d2fc2:~$ exit
logout
```

Following the link to the troubleshooting section, it said to try re-provisioning, which I did by running `vagrant provision` from outside:

> Below you’ll find a list of common errors and their solutions. Most issues are resolved by just provisioning again (by running `./tools/provision` (from `/srv/zulip`) inside the Vagrant guest or equivalently `vagrant provision` from outside).

This took a while, and this time after `vagrant ssh` the command prompt appeared as expected:

```
$ vagrant ssh
Welcome to Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (GNU/Linux 6.10.14-linuxkit aarch64)

This is the Zulip development environment.  Popular commands:
* tools/provision - Update the development environment
* tools/run-dev - Run the development server
* tools/lint - Run the linter (quick and catches many problems)
* tools/test-* - Run tests (use --help to learn about options)

Read https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/testing/testing.html to learn
how to run individual test suites so that you can get a fast debug cycle.

Last login: Thu Dec 26 19:49:38 2024 from 172.17.0.1
(zulip-py3-venv) vagrant@8549f73d2fc2:/srv/zulip$ 
```

(With `(zulip-py3-venv)` this time.)

**Chris Bobbe** · 2024-12-26 20:10 UTC

So overall the process was pretty smooth and I think I'm all set now. I'm just wondering if we can have it fail early and not say "Machine already provisioned" when the `zulip-py3-venv` part isn't set up yet.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 22:37 UTC

I think it's Vagrant itself that produces that "already provisioned" message. It is a bit puzzling, though, that it marks the VM as already provisioned even if the previous attempt to provision failed. That could reflect something we're doing wrong with exit codes or something.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 22:38 UTC

Here's the `Vagrantfile` configuration:
```
  config.vm.provision "shell",
    # We want provision to be run with the permissions of the vagrant user.
    privileged: false,
    path: "tools/setup/vagrant-provision",
    env: { "UBUNTU_MIRROR" => ubuntu_mirror }
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 22:38 UTC

It seems like this should set a failed exit status when failing.
```
$ cat tools/setup/vagrant-provision 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -x
set -e
set -o pipefail
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 22:39 UTC

So I'm a bit puzzled.

I think the other thing we could do better here is improving where we advertise this step:

(replying to Chris Bobbe)
> There was a helpful note in our setup doc, which I followed: > **Important note**: There is a [known upstream issue on macOS](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/provision.20error.20ERR_PNPM_LINKING_FAILED/near/1649241) that can cause provisioning to fail with `ERR_PNPM_LI …

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 22:39 UTC

To preempt the failure mode, rather than giving it as a solution after you've already hit a failure. Whether that's a good idea I guess depends on whether we think the upstream bug will ever be fixed as well as whether the `osxfs (legacy` filesystem configuration has material downsides.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-02 18:58 UTC

Usually the recommend workflow when switching branches it to:
- Check out the branch.
- Rebase the branch onto `upstream/main`. (It's generally easiest to always work on top of `main` to avoid expensive re-provisioning that happens when you move your Git tree backwards in time)
- Run `tools/provision` to make sure the development environment has the right dependencies installed for that version.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-02 18:59 UTC

You definitely should never need to do a `vagrant destroy`; and you should get a warning if you try to run `test-backend` without first provisioning if it matters.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-02 19:00 UTC

I'm not sure how it's possible that you'd see old results from a previous test run, unless you'd not actually switched branches as you'd intended. What precise commands are you using?

**Maneesh Shukla** · 2025-01-02 19:06 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> I'm not sure how it's possible that you'd see old results from a previous test run, unless you'd not actually switched branches as you'd intended. What precise commands are you using?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 22:35 UTC

`tools/provision --force` is much more likely to be a good use of time than `vagrant destroy`. Destroying the VM is going to force you to re-download all the dependencies, and should do nothing useful that much faster tools like force-provisioning or `tools/rebuild-*` can do.

## Hot reloading on Mac.

*2025-01-30 to 2025-09-09 · 17 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/Hot.20reloading.20on.20Mac.2E/with/2068591)*

Is it mentioned in the documentation how to set up hot reloading on Mac?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-31 00:13 UTC

I don't think so. Ideally, it should just work, but I imagine that the problem is something of the flavour "Nothing notifies the container at all when you save changes in your editor outside the container". 

I'd search for editor plugins for use with Vagrant.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-02-06 16:34 UTC

We have [documented this](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-recommended.html#vscode-setup-optional) for VS Code.

Any solution/progress on this one?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-09-04 18:57 UTC

Not that I'm aware of. I think #**documentation>edits not appearing with vagrant** seems likely to be broadly the same problem, though, so we should spend some attention on it.

**Sayed Mahmood Sayedi** · 2025-09-04 19:57 UTC

Yeah, that would be nice to have solved. The [VSCode setup](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-recommended.html#vscode-setup-optional) resolves the "hot reloading" issue for me, but other configurations, such as `.gitconfig`, do not work. **Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-09-05 10:17 UTC

**Maneesh Shukla** · 2025-09-05 14:50 UTC

Oh, so finally I got this from docs.
> **Important note**: There is a [known upstream issue on macOS](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/provision.20error.20ERR_PNPM_LINKING_FAILED/near/1649241) that can cause provisioning to fail with `ERR_PNPM_LINKING_FAILED` or other errors. The temporary fix is to open the …
I changed to `osxfs` but I didn't revert it to `VirtioFS` after provisioning.

Today I deleted everything and completed a fresh setup of Zulip and this para helped me.
So, for hot-reloading to work, you need to revert to `VirtioFS` after provisioning.

**Sayed Mahmood Sayedi** · 2025-09-05 16:14 UTC

Interesting, that works perfectly fine. Thanks for the fix.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-09-05 16:15 UTC

Maybe this deserves a mention in the docs?

**Sayed Mahmood Sayedi** · 2025-09-05 16:15 UTC

I think so.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-05 16:15 UTC

For several releases of Docker and macOS now, I have not had to fiddle with the file-system settings in Docker. YMMV.

**Maneesh Shukla** · 2025-09-05 17:01 UTC

(replying to Maneesh Shukla)
> Back in Docker, you can return to using VirtioFS for better system performance while developing
Instead of better system performance, we can specifically mention the term `hot-reloading.`

**Sayed Mahmood Sayedi** · 2025-09-05 17:07 UTC

(replying to Karl Stolley)
> For several releases of Docker and macOS now, I have not had to fiddle with the file-system settings in Docker. YMMV.

Doing the provision again without changing the file-system settings to `osxfs (legacy)` and then back to the default (`VirtioFS`), it finishes without any issue for me. So I think it would also be good to mention in the docs that this step is only necessary if things are not working properly. Right now, it reads as if it is a necessary step for provisioning to work.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-09-09 19:06 UTC

We might want to also make the docs recommend posting somewhere if you have to do it. It's possible that macOS fixed their bug.

getting so slow speed when cloning like 16kib/s ? any solution for it??

**Hazem Ahmed** · 2025-02-08 19:37 UTC

First, check your internet connection to ensure it’s stable.

Here are some solutions that might help:
1. easiest option is to download the ZIP file 
2. try a different protocol switch between HTTPS and SSH
3. use a shallow clone it will reduce the amount of data downloaded by cloning only the latest commit

```

## provisioning multiple versions

*2025-02-20 to 2025-02-20 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/provisioning.20multiple.20versions/with/2097610)*

**Zixuan James Li** · 2025-02-20 18:43 UTC

Is there a general approach to switch back and forth between an older server and a new one, without needing to re-provision every time? I think cloning zulip/zulip twice, checking out different revisions, and having two vagrant machines should work, but is there a better way?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-20 18:47 UTC

Two independent checkouts is one reasonable way. Another option is to use an open community self-hosted server, like for Lichess or Outreachy. A remote development droplet is the other, I think.

As I understand it, this happens because Podman's output is different from Docker, which confuses Vagrant (on my system, `docker` executable is a symlink to `podman`). I tried googling the error verbatim (``Vagrant received unknown output from `docker build` while building a container``), but didn't find anything of note.

I'd appreciate any help with this problem.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-04-07 21:25 UTC

I have not tried this, but it sounds like a Vagrant upstream issue that you’ll need to figure out. Start by making sure you have the latest version of Vagrant.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-04-07 21:28 UTC

It’s possible that the `UBUNTU_MIRROR` warning, which would ordinarily be harmless, is confusing whatever regex Vagrant uses to parse the output; you can try [specifying an Ubuntu mirror](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-recommended.html#specifying-an-ubuntu-mirror).

**Dmytro Khorsun** · 2025-04-07 21:33 UTC

I'm running Vagrant 2.4.3, which is the latest version.

After going through all podman-related github issues, it appears that Vagrant just doesn't support Podman: https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/issues/12378#issuecomment-847114495

I guess I'll have to install Docker... Having two different container runtimes on the same machine will certainly be [Fun](https://dwarffortresswiki.org/index.php?title=Fun&redirect=no).

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-05-25 17:08 UTC

My guess is that you are using an existing WSL environment.
We recommend setting up a [fresh new instance](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-recommended.html#:~:text=a%20fresh%20distribution%20is%20recommended%20if%20you%20previously%20installed%20other%20software%20in%20your%20WSL%20environment%20that%20might%20conflict%20with%20the%20Zulip%20environment) for Zulip development to avoid such conflicts. 

You can see this [article](https://cloudbytes.dev/snippets/how-to-install-multiple-instances-of-ubuntu-in-wsl2) to be able to do that. 

I faced the `node: bad option` error sometime back:

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-09 18:17 UTC

Well there's a question of how that got deleted. But structurally `scripts/lib/node_cache.py` is the code wrapping `pnpm install` that installs that, and probably running that again the right way will fix it for you.

I'm running into an issue while provisioning Zulip using Vagrant with the Docker provider on macOS. But I consistently get this error:

```zsh

/tmp/vagrant-shell: line 49: /srv/zulip/tools/provision: Operation not permitted

Just to follow the guidelines, here's all the relevant info:
* **Host OS:** macOS Sequoia 15.5
* **Installation method:** Vagrant (Docker provider)
* **Proxy:** Not using a proxy.

**What I’ve tried so far:**
* Confirmed executable permissions on `tools/provision`
* Seems to be a macOS Docker volume mount permission issue
* I have already setup docker to `osxfs (legacy)`


**Full error log**
```zsh

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-27 17:25 UTC

Search for `vagrant docker macos "Operation not permitted"` in your favorite search engine and you'll get some suggestions. My guess it it's an permissions issue where the user running Vagrant doesn't have enough OS permissions. I would not recommend switching to the NFS sharing model.

**Sujal Shah** · 2025-06-27 18:34 UTC

## ✔ Provisioning failure when Linux username is "zulip"

*2026-01-14 to 2026-01-21 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20Provisioning.20failure.20when.20Linux.20username.20is.20.22zulip.22/with/2352976)*

**Aarush Jain** · 2026-01-14 14:15 UTC

Hi everyone! I encountered a specific edge case while running `./tools/provision` on a local WSL2 environment where my Linux username is `zulip`.
**The Issue:** The script `tools/setup/postgresql-init-dev-db` fails with the following error: `ERROR: role "zulip" is a member of role "zulip"` `Subcommand failed with exit status 3: tools/setup/postgresql-init-dev-db`
**The Cause:** Because my system `whoami` is `zulip`, the script attempts to execute: `GRANT $USERNAME TO "$VAGRANTUSERNAME";` which evaluates to `GRANT zulip TO "zulip";`. PostgreSQL rejects this as a circular redundancy.
**My Workaround:** I manually edited `tools/setup/postgresql-init-dev-db` to wrap the `GRANT` statement in a conditional check:

Bash

```
if [ "$USERNAME" != "$VAGRANTUSERNAME" ]; then
    # ... GRANT logic ...
fi
```

This allowed provisioning to complete successfully. Has anyone else encountered this? It might be worth adding this check to the setup script for users who name their local dev environment accounts "zulip".

**Sachin Kumar** · 2026-03-26 13:10 UTC

Update: Finally got Codespaces fully working end-to-end!

Hi @Greg Price and team,

My friend and I spent some time digging deep into why `./tools/provision` fails on a fresh GitHub Codespace. The good news is, we managed to fix everything and got a flawless Zulip dev environment running! 

Codespaces behave a bit differently than a standard VM. We found 6 specific things that break the script. Here is the simple breakdown of the issues and how we bypassed them:

**1. The first `apt-get update` crashes:** The default Codespace image has an expired security key for Yarn. This breaks the update process immediately. *Fix:* We just need the script to delete that broken `yarn.list` file if it detects a Codespace environment.

**2. Node.js setup conflicts:** Codespaces already has `pnpm` and `yarn` installed globally. When Zulip's script tries to set them up using `corepack`, it refuses to overwrite the existing ones and fails. *Fix:* Force-delete those pre-existing files right before running the corepack setup.

**3. PyICU linking issue (`libicu73` vs `libicu74` conflict):** Codespaces has some pre-installed Python environments that leak conflicting variables into the build path. When the script tries to build PyICU from source, it picks up these wrong paths and links to an older `libicui18n.so.73` instead of the Ubuntu 24.04 system's new `libicui18n.so.74`. This mismatch later causes Django to crash with an `ImportError`. *Fix:* Unset those conflicting environment variables before the build so pip strictly uses the system's `pkg-config` path.

**4. Services don't start automatically:** Unlike a normal Linux machine, background services like PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ don't start on their own in the container. *Fix:* The script just needs to explicitly start them in the background.

**5. Python 3.12 virtual environment changes:** Zulip’s `setup_path.py` looks for a file called `activate_this.py`. The catch is, fresh Python 3.12 virtual environments don't create this file anymore! This breaks Django imports. *Fix:* We updated the script to detect the virtual environment path dynamically instead of relying on that missing file.

**6. PostgreSQL Init Sudo Prompt:** During the PostgreSQL setup, the script runs a `sudo` command. The Codespace pauses to ask for a password, and since it's an automated script, it fails after 3 tries. *Fix:* Running a quick `sudo -v` beforehand prevents the prompt.

I have local fixes tested for all of these! What is the best way to share these changes with the team? Should I open one big PR for Codespace support, or break them down into smaller, separate PRs?

Would love to help make this seamless for future beginners!

> **5. Python 3.12 virtual environment changes:** Zulip’s `setup_path.py` looks for a file called `activate_this.py`. The catch is, fresh Python 3.12 virtual environments don't create this file anymore! This breaks Django imports. *Fix:* We updated the script to detect the virtual environment path dyn …

This is an odd claim. We manage our virtual environment with `uv`, which always creates `activate_this.py`. If you’re manually creating a virtual environment some other way, you’re going to run into a lot of problems (especially in the future as we continue to more closely integrate `uv`).

**Sachin Kumar** · 2026-03-27 05:08 UTC

Ah, you're totally right! I just tested it in the Codespace. A standard `python3 -m venv` skips `activate_this.py` in 3.12, but `uv` handles it perfectly.

Turns out the VS Code Python extension was jumping the gun—it was auto-creating a standard venv in the background before `./tools/provision` even had a chance to run and set it up properly with `uv`.

I'm reverting that hacky workaround in `setup_path.py` right now. Instead, I'll just disable `python.createEnvironment.trigger` in `devcontainer.json`. That should stop VS Code from interfering and ensure we strictly rely on the `uv` setup.

Thanks for the catch! I'll update the PR in a bit.

Hey everyone! I've updated the PR for GitHub Codespaces support based on the recent feedback: PR Link - [#38678](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38678)

The provisioning changes are now strictly isolated behind the `CODESPACES` environment variable, so standard setups are 100% untouched. All the main backend and frontend tests are passing cleanly!

Just a quick heads-up: the `Ubuntu 22.04 production build` job is failing, but looking at the logs, it seems to be an unrelated upstream issue with the recent `uv` migration (the release script is accidentally evaluating package names as bash commands).

The PR is ready for another look whenever someone has a moment. Thanks!

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-03-29 23:05 UTC

**Sachin Kumar** · 2026-03-31 09:31 UTC

Hi @Anders Kaseorg ,

You were right, and I'm sorry for jumping ahead without checking the CI logs properly. I should've looked more carefully before making that assumption. I'll be more careful next time.

Anyway, I spent the last few hours digging deeper into the Codespaces provisioning issues, and everything is now working end-to-end with no manual steps needed.

Here's what was broken and how I fixed it:

**PyICU version/linking mismatch** --> The default Codespace image has pre-installed Python/Conda environments that were leaking conflicting variables into the build path. This caused PyICU to link against an older `libicu` instead of the system one, throwing a fatal `ImportError`. Fixed by unsetting those variables (`CONDA_PREFIX`, `VIRTUAL_ENV`, etc.) before the provision script runs.

**RabbitMQ hostname resolution** --> Codespaces can't resolve their own hostname during RabbitMQ setup. Fixed by injecting `127.0.0.1 $(hostname)` into `/etc/hosts` through the `postCreateCommand` in `.devcontainer.json`.

**PostgreSQL authentication** --> The provisioning script was hitting a password prompt when running `sudo -i -u postgres` in a fresh Codespace, which broke the automated flow. Worked around this by giving the `vscode` user passwordless sudo access for Postgres beforehand.

**Services not starting** --> Codespaces don't auto-start services via `systemd`, so `postgresql`, `rabbitmq-server`, `redis`, and `memcached` were never coming up. Added an explicit startup block in `provision_inner.py`, gated behind a `CODESPACES=true` environment check.

With all this sorted, we no longer need to skip the dev database build. Migrations run, the database gets populated in the background, and a new contributor can open a Codespace and go straight to `./tools/run-dev`.

[PR#38678](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38678) is updated with the commits. Thanks again for pushing back earlier, it made me actually look at what was going wrong instead of guessing.

You can also pick up the issue from [CZO](https://chat.zulip.org/#recent) and be up-to-date on Zulip's GitHub with a PR labeled `Help wanted`.

And if the contributor of the existing PR is not active, you can message him and ask whether he is continuing with it, or if I should do it?

Happy contributing :smiling_face:

## macOS provision mounts zulip directory at unexpected path

*2026-08-11 to 2026-08-12 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/21-provision-help/topic/macOS.20provision.20mounts.20zulip.20directory.20at.20unexpected.20path/with/2507734)*

**Luke Faraone** · 2026-08-11 02:09 UTC

@Emily Sutherlin had her Zulip code repository at `~/zulip/zulip`, I had her move it to `~/zulip` per guide. 

This required us to tear down and recreate the docker container;`vagrant provision` succeeds, but when she `vagrant ssh`es, we found ourselves landing in `/Users/emilysutherlin/zulip` in the container. `/srv/zulip` did not exist in the container. Activating the venv did not succeed because the venv did not exist at the expected path. We symlinked `/Users/emilysutherlin/zulip` to `/srv/zulip` which "fixed" the venv but `check_venv()` doesn't like that.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-08-11 09:55 UTC

Maybe try `VirtioFS` file sharing in docker settings?

**Luke Faraone** · 2026-08-12 00:02 UTC

So pragmatically, that would be:
```sh
vagrant ssh
# Inside the container now, remove the symbolic link we created earlier
unlink /srv/zulip
logout
```
then open the Docker Desktop app, go to Settings, find "Choose file sharing implementation for your containers", and change the value to "VirtIOFS"? (this is my Settings window, for illustrative purposes)
![Docker Desktop 2026-08-11 at 12.58.32.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/81/9yg2OMZwseL8eBJuqBbX5YJ5/Docker-Desktop-2026-08-11-at-12.58.32.png)

Then
```sh
vagrant provision
vagrant ssh
# expected result: user lands in /srv/zulip? 
```

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-08-12 04:42 UTC

I would suggest installing the latest version of docker, destroying the existing volume and then doing the development setup from start. Make sure you are on `upstream/main` before running provision.
